articles.title: LSU student says she was raped by a football player who is still on the team
articles.summary: “LSU does really protect their athletes, especially their football players,” says the woman, whose claims are being investigated by the local district attorn...
articles.body:
A Louisiana State University student who claims a school football player raped her last year is speaking out about how the school handled her report and the lack of guidance she said she received throughout the process.

Kendall Danielle Francis talked on TikTok about the monthslong Title IX investigation that played out after she reported the October rape to the school. Two days into the current semester, she said, she received an email while she was in class to notify her that the student, who had been suspended for two semesters, had his punishment modified upon appeal to four semesters' probation. He would remain on campus and could continue to play football, she said.

"Now I am just trying to speak on my story, because LSU does really protect their athletes, especially their football players," Francis, who was 18 at the time of the alleged incident, said in the Sept. 14 social media post. As a result of the student's remaining on campus, Francis said, she moved her classes online.

Francis wasn't aware that filing the Title IX complaint was a separate process from filing criminal charges, a spokesperson for Francis said Wednesday.

"When she filed for Title IX, they [the university] did not tell her she could also contact the police and have them launch a criminal investigation," a spokesperson said. "She just assumed LSU would do the criminal investigation."

Francis' post, however, caught the attention of East Baton Rouge Parish District Attorney Hillar Moore, whose office announced it was launching a criminal investigation. He has requested "all reports, interviews, evidence, and other relevant records" from LSU, the university police and the Baton Rouge Police Department, as well as the coroner's office, which handles the evidence collection from sexual assault victims.

"This is now an open criminal investigation," Moore said Sept. 22 in a statement on his agency's Facebook page .

Francis' allegations come as accusations that members of a fraternity gang-raped a female Cornell University student for several hours have renewed questions nationwide about whether universities are doing enough to protect students from sexual assault.

LSU President Wade Rousse said in a statement that the university is cooperating with investigators.

"Let me assure everyone that this incident has been handled professionally and that LSU has strictly followed our policies, procedures and best practices, including the Title IX process, to guide our actions to date," Rousse said.

Title IX is a federal law that requires all universities that receive federal funds to put safeguards in place to protect students from sexual predators.

Francis didn't respond to several reach-outs from NBC News to discuss her online allegations or share the findings of the Title IX investigation.

In her TikTok video , Francis said she was assaulted at around 4:30 a.m. Oct. 18 "by a football player at LSU."

"That day basically changed my life," she said, adding that she "developed pretty severe anxiety" and that after an official diagnosis she began taking medication to manage it.

Francis said that she was taken to the hospital, where she had "a rape kit done," but that she didn't initially press charges.

"However, I did go through the Title IX process here at LSU, which took a really, really long time," she said.

Francis said she returned to school assuming the football player was suspended and under investigation by the police. She said she was in a class when she was notified via email that the alleged attacker was still "accountable" for the rape and would be on probation and allowed to attend classes on campus and play football.

"I was under the impression that because LSU found him responsible that LSU would do their part, that criminal charges, you know, would be pursued," Francis said in an interview last week with WAFB-TV of Baton Rouge .

Universities are generally not required to automatically alert the police when a Title IX sexual assault or rape investigation is underway, especially if the survivor requests confidentiality or chooses not to involve law enforcement.

Francis said in a second TikTok post that she reported the alleged rape this month to LSU police in an attempt to press charges. NBC News has reached out to the agency to confirm that, but so far there has been no response.

The Baton Rouge-based newspaper The Advocate reported that it had obtained the Title IX documents from the case and that they confirm Francis' assertion that the football player was found responsible for the rape.

Those documents, according to the newspaper, also confirm that his punishment was reduced on appeal from a two-semester suspension to four semesters of probation.

Some of the sexual activity between Francis and the football player was consensual, according to those documents as reported by The Advocate. Still, the football player admitted that he didn't specifically ask for Francis' consent before they had intercourse "and did not stop when he later asked and she was silent," according to the Title IX documents.

Meg Casper Sunstrom, an LSU spokesperson, didn't confirm the outcome of the Title IX proceedings or the discipline that was handed down to the student. Nor did she respond to questions about whether the football player was at LSU and playing for the team.

"Since there was no criminal complaint filed by the victim, LSU appropriately turned the issue over to our Title IX office as mandated by law," Sunstrom said in an email.

But she noted that the football player did "self-report" an incident involving his accuser with the LSU Police Department.

Dated Oct. 18, 2025, the report, obtained from LSU via a public records request, said the 19-year-old football player was at the school's football facility when he called police "due to concerns about potential accusations from the other party."

The report gave no indication what those potential accusations were.

The incident report says the football player told police that Francis had told him she was mentally unwell and had "thoughts of suicidal ideation."

The responding officer noted in the report that police had been in touch with Francis four days earlier, on Oct. 14, "regarding a similar incident." An officer determined that Francis posed no danger to herself and "seemed to be commenting out of spite."

This time, the report says, when police went to Francis' on-campus residence, "it was evident that Francis's mental state was unstable." The report doesn't detail the basis for that conclusion.

"She agreed to go to the hospital for further evaluation, and I transported her to Baton Rouge General Hospital for assessment," the responding officer wrote in his report.

Francis said in her TikTok post that she dreads the possibility of running into her alleged attacker on campus.

"So that made my anxiety really, really bad, because I don't want to face this person," she said. "I really just wanted to bring awareness upon this situation, because I'm just dealing with a lot right now, and I think that this story needs to be heard."

articles.title: 3 Takeaways From the Maple Leafs 2-1 Win Over the Islanders
articles.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs landed their first win of the season, 24 hours after dropping their season opener at home. The post 3 Takeaways From the Maple Leafs...
articles.body:
The Maple Leafs needed a response after Tuesday's disappointing opening-night loss to the Montreal Canadiens .

Toronto defeated the New York Islanders 2-1 on Wednesday night, getting goals from Colton Sissons and Easton Cowan before hanging on through a tense third period. The Maple Leafs were outshot by the Islanders 27-26 but, more importantly, looked considerably more structured defensively than they had 24 hours earlier.

A brutal defensive mistake in the third period allowed the Islanders to get on the board shorthanded, and suddenly what had looked like a comfortable two-goal lead became a one-goal game.

But the Maple Leafs found a way to close it out.

Here are three takeaways from Toronto's first win of the 2026-27 season.

Easton Cowan Looks Ready for a Bigger Role

Easton Cowan had the kind of game the Maple Leafs desperately needed from one of their young players.

He finished with two points, assisting on Sissons' opening goal before scoring Toronto's second goal on the power play.

The power-play goal was particularly important.

Cowan found himself in a dangerous position and made no mistake when the opportunity arrived, giving Toronto a 2-0 lead late in the first period.

His assist on Sissons' goal was just as encouraging. Cowan helped create the opening before Nick Paul and Sissons finished the play, giving him a hand in both of Toronto's goals.

That's exactly what the Maple Leafs need from him.

The trade of Matthew Knies to Columbus left Toronto with a much different-looking left side, and Cowan entered the season with an opportunity to take on a larger role. NHL.com had him projected on the third line against the Islanders, but his performance could force Jim Hiller to give him more responsibility sooner rather than later.

Cowan isn't going to suddenly become a 30-goal scorer because of one game.

But he is showing signs that he can become an important offensive piece for the Maple Leafs.

And Wednesday was a heck of a start. He earned the game's second star.

Anthony Stolarz Gives Toronto Exactly What It Needed

If Cowan provided the offense, Anthony Stolarz provided the insurance.

Stolarz stopped all 20 shots he faced before the Islanders finally broke through with a shorthanded goal in the third period.

That was the kind of performance the Maple Leafs needed after Tuesday.

Toronto's defensive execution was hardly flawless. There were still moments when the Islanders generated pressure, particularly as the game tightened in the third period.

The Maple Leafs turned the puck over in their own end while trying to move it up ice, with Darren Raddysh making the key misplay that ultimately allowed Emil Heineman to score shorthanded.

But it shouldn't overshadow what came before it.

Stolarz was excellent, and several of his saves kept the Islanders from turning Toronto's mistakes into goals. The Maple Leafs couldn't afford another night in which their goaltender was left fighting an uphill battle.

This time, Stolarz gave them the type of performance that allowed the rest of the team to survive its mistakes.

The Maple Leafs Penalty Kill Was Outstanding

The Maple Leafs also deserve plenty of credit for what they did when they went shorthanded.

Toronto killed off both Islanders power plays, keeping New York off the scoreboard on the man advantage.

That might not sound particularly dramatic, but it became increasingly important as the game progressed.

The Maple Leafs had a two-goal lead for most of the night. Every penalty created another opportunity for the Islanders to change the momentum.

That is a significant improvement from the type of defensive performance the team wanted to clean up after Tuesday's loss. The Maple Leafs were more willing to block shots, clear rebounds and make the simple play when they needed to.

They finished with 16 blocked shots compared to 11 for New York, another indication that the defensive effort was considerably more committed.

The shorthanded goal was certainly a blemish.

But outside of that one disastrous sequence, the Maple Leafs did what they needed to do.

They got timely scoring from Cowan, a brilliant performance from Stolarz and a perfect night from the penalty kill.

After opening the season with a loss, that's exactly the kind of bounce-back performance Toronto needed.

articles.title: Michigan football news: John Henry Daley, Andrew Marsh on injury report
articles.summary: Michigan football enters its next Big Ten test with several important health questions hanging over the Wolverines. As Michigan prepares for a matchup with M...
articles.body:
Michigan football enters its next Big Ten test with several important health questions hanging over the Wolverines . As Michigan prepares for a matchup with Minnesota , John Henry Daley and Andrew Marsh headline a loaded injury report. That could significantly influence the team's approach Saturday.

Daley is Michigan's leading edge rusher with three sacks and 11 pressures. He is listed as questionable after suffering a lower-body injury late in the Wolverines' loss to Iowa . The encouraging development is that Daley has been walking without a boot or crutches. His availability would provide a major boost to a Michigan defense preparing for another conference challenge.

Marsh, meanwhile, is also questionable. That leaves another key offensive piece uncertain heading into the weekend. Marsh leads the team with 22 catches for a total of receiving 239 yards so far. The Wolverines are additionally monitoring edge rusher Dom Nichols and offensive lineman Andrew Sprague. They both carry 'questionable' designations. There is better news along the offensive line, with Blake Frazier listed as probable and trending toward availability.

Michigan enters the matchup at 3–1 overall and 0–1 in Big Ten play under head coach Kyle Whittingham. The Wolverines opened with a 13–12 win over Western Michigan . They stunned No. 11 Oklahoma 17–10 and cruised past UTEP 52–17. That was before suffering a narrow 20–19 home loss to No. 17 Iowa . Quarterback Bryce Underwood and wide receiver JJ Buchanan lead their offense. Now, Michigan needs a bounce-back performance against Minnesota. Getting its questionable contributors cleared could be critical as the Wolverines look to reclaim momentum and strengthen their conference standing.

articles.title: Recap: Opening night mayhem leads to 8-4 Avalanche win
articles.summary: The power play giveth and the power play taketh.
articles.body:
For the first game out of 84 in the 2026-27 season the Colorado Avalanche hosted the LA Kings at Ball Arena and it won't soon be forgotten. A 8-4 rout of the Kings saw multiple power play and shorthanded goals against for Colorado and even a Nathan MacKinnon fight.

Believe it or not but the power play got the Avalanche on the board first, however in pure hilarious fashion it was the second unit that got the job done. Brock Nelson deflected a rebound off of Kings goaltender Darcy Kuemper 's mask and into the net. The Kings then got their own power play and didn't score on it but seemed to give them momentum. After a couple big saves from Mackenzie Blackwood and good pings, Los Angeles finally broke through. It was defenseman Brian Dumoulin who got a shot through traffic to even the score. The next Kings power play didn't go well either but Parker Kelly got a strike on a breakaway just after the penalty expired to put Colorado up by one heading into the first intermission.

A five-on-three for Colorado carried over into the second frane and the boys in burgundy made it count as Nathan MacKinnon lit the lamp just 23 seconds into the period. Just one minute later, though, Joel Armia got one back for the Kings shorthanded when he beat Blackwood from distance. At 3-2 was the closest the Kings got because the Avalanche added two more scores in the second period. First, again from MacKinnon and then Nic Roy. On the latter goal Jaden Schwartz was lying open the crease making contact with Kuemper but the Kings didn't even try to challenge the goal so Colorado was up 5-3 at that point.

But, not so fast. Los Angeles got their second shorthanded goal of the period when Trevor Moore put a snipe on Blackwood. The Avalanche responded when the second power play unit was put back on the ice to finish out the man advantage and Artturi Lehkonen converted from the slot. So the Avalanche were back up by three with a 6-3 score going into the second intermission.

On a particularly bad shift for Josh Manson halfway through the third period where he lost the puck leading to extended offensive zone time for Los Angeles and then took a penalty, it was Artemi Panarin who scored from distance through traffic on the delayed penalty to put the fourth Kings goal on the board.

If ten goals wasn't exciting enough, there was a Nathan MacKinnon fight against Kings defenseman Brandt Clarke . The Avalanche superstar was the instigator and even landed a few rights in the process. There was still ten minutes to go after the brawl and Gabe Landeskog scored his first goal of the season on rebound after Cale Makar drove to the net. For the eighth and final tally Lehkonen got another power play goal with the second unit and the game finally arrived at a 8-4 Avalanche final.

There was just about everything in this game from good and bad goaltending, power play goals galore and even a couple shorties. It showed the sloppy nature of this game that counted for the first time in September in Avalanche history. There will be a lot of days off this month to tighten up some mistakes and mishaps while building on early successes.

Special teams were certainly special this evening. On one hand the Avalanche got four power play goals, yet gave up two shorthanded. The first unit only converted on a five-on-three and the second unit carried the load with a trio of their own. Two functional power play groups would be ideal but how long is it going to last before just heavily favoring the first unit again?

One more game at home against the St. Louis Blues starting at 7 p.m. MT on Saturday, October 3rd.

articles.title: What punishment do rival Premier League clubs want for Manchester City?
articles.summary: A number of Premier League clubs believe a points deduction that would relegate Manchester City to the Championship for one season would be insufficient.Give...
articles.body:
A number of Premier League clubs believe a points deduction that would relegate Manchester City to the Championship for one season would be insufficient.

Given the scale of City's offences, these clubs want a sanction that will result in a prolonged absence from the English top-flight ( The Guardian ).

The independent commission that found them guilty of the rule breaches will determine their punishment at a sanctions hearing.

The Citizens have confirmed they will appeal against the damning findings.

The appeal hearing, per the league's new rules, must be concluded within 12 weeks of being filed.

But City could delay the process by arguing the new rules should not apply as they were introduced this season while the charges against them are historic.

Man City have dominated English football since Sheikh Mansoor's takeover in 2008, winning 22 major trophies including eight Premier League titles and a Champions League.

But now their reputation is on the line after being found guilty of all charges related to breaches of financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

If their appeal fails, the club could be fined, docked points or even expelled from the competition altogether.

articles.title: Liverpool told what it will take to sign 'outstanding' star from arch-rivals
articles.summary: Liverpool are currently sixth in the Premier League. This means that, at the moment, they're sitting outside of the Champions League spots which is far from...
articles.body:
Liverpool are currently sixth in the Premier League.

This means that, at the moment, they're sitting outside of the Champions League spots which is far from ideal.

Last term, Arne Slot led his men to a fifth-place finish and, in a normal campaign, qualifying for Europe's premium competition would have been the bare minimum but, just a season after winning the Premier League title, fans wanted to see their team at least try and defend it.

This obviously didn't end up happening which is why Slot was relieved of his duties and why Liverpool had to spend another £150 million on new players.

Andoni Iraola was the man chosen to take over and, while his impact on the squad has been fairly impressive, more can come from the Anfield outfit.

And, at the moment, fans need more so that they know that their club are going to be able to handle themselves by the end of the term.

However, since their squad depth is so thin, it's unclear whether they'll make it all the way to the end or not which is why transfers are already being mooted in January.

Everton want £80 million for Jarrad Branthwaite

Even though Liverpool focused on improving their defence in the summer, some cracks are still showing.

Jeremy Jacquet , Virgil van Dijk and Ronald Araujo have all helped shore up the Reds' back line massively and, without this trio among their ranks, Liverpool would be so much worse off.

However, left-back is a different story altogether with neither Kostas Tsimikas nor Milos Kerkez meeting the standards expected of them.

But, since Van Dijk 's current Liverpool contract is set to expire in June 2027, his future is undecided.

And, while Liverpool's fans will almost certainly want the Dutchman to stay, it does feel like Liverpool will need to have a succession plan in place just in case their captain doesn't stay on.

That's why this latest update from Football Insider on Everton's valuation of Jarrad Branthwaite will certainly pique the interest of Liverpool's fanbase.

"Everton still believe that centre-back Jarrad Branthwaite is an £80million player, sources have told Football Insider," they wrote .

"The Toffees have no plans to cash in on the 24-year-old, and still regard him as one of the Premier League's best defenders when he is fit.

"Sources say that while the Merseysiders do not want to lose the defender, they are confident that he will net them an eye-watering sum one day.

"Former Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider last week that Liverpool are working on a shock move to sign Branthwaite next summer.

"The ex-recruitment chief outlined that the Reds have had scouts watching the defender at the Hill Dickinson S tad ium on several occasions of late.

"Brown made it clear that Liverpool are doing their "due diligence" on Branthwaite, and believe he "ticks a lot of boxes" as a potential replacement for Virgil van Dijk."

Liverpool signing Jarrad Branthwaite would be unreal for them

One thing that rarely ever happens is Liverpool and Everton conducting transfer business with one another.

Although both teams are often at opposite ends of the Premier League table to one another, their rivalry is still fierce with both sets of fans looking forward to their fixtures each season.

And, even though a deal for Ndiaye is now off the table thanks to him joining Manchester City , a deal for the English centre-back could certainly brighten the mood at Anfield if Van Dijk chooses to exit.

Indeed, the " outstanding " defender's injury history is a tad worrying but, since he's managed to stay fit since the start of the 2026-27 season, there's hope that he's now grown out of that stage in his career.

Branthwaite is still only 24 years old so he has plenty of time to grow into an even better player and, if he's wanting to challenge for silverware and not move too far away from his current home, where better is there for him to go than L4?

Here's hoping that these rumours are true and Liverpool actually try and agree a deal with their rivals for him.

articles.title: Bears news: Chicago's LT situation murky again with new injury update
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears secured a dominant 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football, but the win came with a troubling setback along the...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears secured a dominant 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football, but the win came with a troubling setback along the offensive line. Starting left tackle Braxton Jones exited the contest with a knee injury, and head coach Ben Johnson confirmed that Jones is now considered week-to-week.

Jones played a pivotal role in Chicago's impressive 2-1 start to the 2026 regular season, providing steady protection on the perimeter. Before his departure, the Bears offense executed efficiently against Philadelphia's defensive front, accumulating 375 total net yards and holding the ball for nearly 37 minutes. Losing Jones creates a glaring hole on the blind side right as Chicago prepares for a Week 4 matchup against the New York Jets .

Filling that vacancy is not a simple task. Offensive tackle Ozzy Trapilo continues working his way back from his own injury, but his status for Sunday remains up in the air. Addressing Trapilo's timeline, Johnson admitted that the blocker is "getting closer," though he cautioned, "I don't know if this will be the week or not."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

If Trapilo cannot play, Chicago must get creative with its front five. Johnson mentioned that guard Jordan McFadden can play tackle if needed, along with veteran guard Joe Thuney . Backup tackle Theo Benedet stepped in for 17 snaps after Jones went down, but reshuffling position assignments on short notice poses a real test for unit chemistry.

Chicago's offense found plenty of rhythm against Philadelphia, tallying 128 rushing yards led by running back D'Andre Swift's 84-yard performance while quarterback Case Keenum threw for a touchdown. Still, losing Jones forces Johnson into immediate contingency planning. Whether Trapilo returns, McFadden slides outside, or Benedet gets the nod, Chicago must lock down the left tackle spot quickly to keep its offensive momentum intact.

articles.title: Can India, Pakistan be in same group at ODI World Cup 2027? Explaining how World Cup draw is made
articles.summary: How the 2027 ODI World Cup draw will determine whether India and Pakistan are placed in the same group.
articles.body:
The ICC Men's ODI World Cup 2027 features a new format where 14 teams will take part in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.

However, contrary to the last two editions, the ODI World Cup will not start with all participating teams meeting in one league.

The 14 teams will be divided into two groups according to their ranking, before the tournament proceeds into the two-group phase and Super 7.

But it raises a big question for fans - will India and Pakistan play in the same group at 2027 ODI World Cup?

Reports indicate that India and Pakistan may play in the same group in the upcoming World Cup but no official confirmation has been revealed by sources prior to the October 1 announcement of the schedule.

The Sporting News explores how the 2027 World Cup draw will be conducted and whether India and Pakistan will play in the same group.

The 2027 ODI World Cup will consist of 14 teams, although only 12 will qualify directly to the main group stage.

The three lowest-ranked teams out of the 14 qualifying teams will first compete in a three-team Super Series, where each team will face the other two in one match. The winning team will move on to the main stage, while the other two will be knocked out.

The remaining 11 teams along with the winner of the Super Series will thus make up the 12-team main stage.

These 12 teams will be split into two groups of six each, where each team plays five matches against the others in their group. The top three in each group, along with the best fourth-placed team out of the two groups, will make up the Super 7.

When will the ODI World Cup 2027 groups be announced?

The ICC will announce the groups and schedule for the 2027 ODI World Cup on October 1, 2026, with the draw being held in Cape Town at 8:30 p.m. IST.

The draw results will also reveal whether or not India and Pakistan are in the same group.

The 2027 ODI World Cup draw will determine the groups, venues and match dates, with the ICC and Cricket South Africa unveiling the complete fixture list at the Cape Town event on October 1.

The draw comes after the September 30 ODI rankings cut-off, which determines the directly qualified teams. The final group allocation done at random will establish which teams are placed together in the two Round 2 groups.

The 12 teams in Round 2 will be divided into two groups of six each.

The ICC confirmed the group structure but there is no indication whether the allocation will be completely random or use rankings, seeding or predetermined pots.

Therefore, the September 30 ODI rankings should not automatically be interpreted as a seeding order for the Round 2 draw. The official schedule and group announcement on October 1 is expected to provide clarity on how the 12 teams are allocated between the two groups.

Can India, Pakistan be in same group at ODI World Cup 2027?

This all depends on how they will be grouped in the end.

India and Pakistan were drawn in the same group at the last two ODI World Cups, in 2019 and 2023. They also met in the group stage in 2015, while their 2011 meeting was in the semi-finals.

Both nations have qualified for the 2027 World Cup through the ODI rankings and will not play in the Super Series.

Reports stating that India and Pakistan are set to be grouped together in one six-nation group are not officially confirmed as of yet and will only be confirmed when ICC announces the schedule.

If the two teams are indeed grouped together in one group, they will certainly face each other at least once in the group stage itself.

How many times can India play Pakistan at 2027 World Cup?

The new format presents the prospect of up to three India-Pakistan encounters at the 2027 World Cup.

In case the two teams are grouped together and both manage to reach the Super 7 stage, they will get the opportunity to encounter each other during that stage since all the seven teams in the Super 7 stage play against one another.

A third encounter can take place in either the semi-finals or final stages, depending on how the two teams place themselves in the Super 7 rankings. Four teams move forward to the semi-finals; first plays fourth and second plays third.

However, in case they are placed in separate groups, they won't be able to encounter each other in the group stage. They will still have the chance of meeting each other either in the Super 7 stage or in the knockout stage if they both qualify.

Where to watch the 2027 ODI World Cup draw in India

The Star Sports Network will broadcast the World Cup 2027 draw live and it can be live-streamed on JioHotstar app and website.

articles.title: Newcastle: Matthias Jaissle learnt a lot about life after tumour aged five
articles.summary: Newcastle United head coach Matthias Jaissle could not move his neck at one point, but went on to play before embarking on a coaching career that sees him in Tyneside.
articles.body:
"I had a tumour when I was five years old," the Newcastle United head coach says. "Here in my neck so I couldn't move it anymore.

"That was a period where I already learned a lot about life, how important it is to be healthy, and how grateful you can be to be healthy and to follow your dream.

"It was not clear that I could play football as a kid anymore."

He did not elaborate further, but such perspective would be needed.

Jaissle, like so many, visualised one day becoming a professional footballer, but he was among the rare few to actually go on to do so.

The former Hoffenheim defender even felt he was on the verge of a senior call up to the German national team at one stage, only to suffer a serious knee injury.

Jaissle refused to give up, and "kept the dream for a lot longer than the doctors did", but the setback ultimately curtailed his career and he retired a few years later in 2014.

It left him in a dark place, as he previously detailed in an interview with BBC Sport, but the "wounds" he experienced in life have shaped him.

"That makes you the person you are, whatever aspect it is, with the belief you can overcome every obstacle," he says.

"Every setback also has a positive side. If you overcome these challenges then you become stronger, more resilient."

This outlook gave Jaissle a head start in his second career, but he did not necessarily plan on being a coach. Not at first.

Ralf Rangnick, his former manager at Hoffenheim, invited him on to a training programme at RB Leipzig, where his mentor was working at the time, to sample life behind the scenes at the club.

Jaissle was due to be redeployed in a new department every six weeks and started his placement as an assistant youth team coach to ex team-mate Sebastien Hoeness, who now manages Stuttgart.

He was pencilled in to spend time with the club's sporting director and figures from their administrative, commercial and marketing departments.

"I didn't move on," Jaissle says. "After two weeks, wow, I felt joy back in life."

It set Jaissle on the path to Newcastle . He climbed the coaching ladder and won trophies at Austrian side Red Bull Salzburg and Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli.

Players and staff alike were quickly struck by his intensity and work rate.

"Since the first meeting, it was clear this was our guy," a senior Newcastle source says.

'I really love the fans and the people here'

It was still a baptism of fire for the 38-year-old, who had never previously managed in the Premier League, after predecessor Eddie Howe stepped down.

Jaissle insists friend Thomas Tuchel "didn't need to warn" him about what was coming in the top flight, but he had just three weeks to prepare for the visit of Liverpool on the opening weekend and the squad was in flux.

Captain Bruno Guimaraes was about to follow Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali out of the exit door and complete a £75m move to Arsenal at the time.

Although Newcastle would end up making eight signings, they were all aged 24 and under as the club went from having one of the most experienced sides in the Premier League to the youngest almost overnight.

It was a huge amount of change in a short space of time.

There have also been a spate of injuries to key players, but Jaissle has only lost one of his opening seven matches in all competitions, a chastening 4-1 defeat at Leeds United .

"I think there were elements in games where we saw a lot of the things we were looking for," he says. "There were also phases in games where we were not happy and satisfied, so there's still a lot of potential that we can improve."

Jaissle accepts it has been "tougher than expected" to "get stuff into the players' heads" given pre-season was "so short and packed with friendly matches we couldn't change", adding "but considering all these things, we're doing good".

He remains convinced that his aggressive style of play and so-called vertical football will "work anywhere", even if this team is clearly still a work in progress at such an early stage of his reign.

Newcastle have made the most errors leading to shots (12) in the Premier League this season while, at the other end of the field, Jaissle's clinical side have only averaged little more than three efforts on target per match in the top flight.

It feels like there will be ups and downs throughout, given the age of the side, but Jaissle has been struck by the backing of supporters and has quickly settled into life on Tyneside.

He moved out of a hotel into a new home earlier this week and has ventured into the city to sample a handful of restaurants - but only to celebrate wins.

Following the 2-1 victory against Hull City at St James' Park last time out, he even paid for a supporter's birthday meal.

"I really love the fans and the people here," he adds.

articles.title: You are the new Scotland boss - what would you do against North Macedonia?
articles.summary: Put yourself in the shoes of the new Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli as he picks his XI to face North Macedonia.
articles.body:
Nations League: North Macedonia v Scotland

Sebastien Pocognoli is still looking for his first win as Scotland head coach after a goalless draw in Slovenia and Tuesday's bruising 3-0 home defeat by Switzerland.

The Belgian will, however, have high hopes as he takes his side to Skopje considering North Macedonia are the lowest-ranked side in Nations League Group B1 and have already lost to the Swiss and Slovenia.

The 39-year-old had gone into his first, four-game international camp promising to give as many players as possible a chance to impress and on Tuesday made three changes from the opener in Ljubljana.

With Jack Hendry suspended after the centre-half's early red card against the Swiss, at least one change will be enforced against North Macedonia but what other alterations might Pocognoli make and who would you like to feature?

Patterson still excited by two new team bosses

New coach, new players, but same old failings hamper Scotland

Hampden debut to forget but Pocognoli looks at bigger picture

With Al-Ettifaq's Hendry missing out this time, might Pocognoli be tempted to abandon his preferred three-at-the-back system?

That seems unlikely no matter if he thinks North Macedonia will revert to the two up front they had at home to Switzerland or go with one, as they did in Slovenia.

Pocognoli, one imagines, will be keen to give his system another chance to gel considering it effectively had to be abandoned after 10 minutes with Hendry's early dismissal against the Swiss.

Swansea City's Stephen Welsh, who had started in Slovenia, came on as an early substitute on Tuesday, while Dinamo Zagreb's Scott McKenna has played the full 180 minutes over both games and neither have done their reputations any harm.

Brondy's Luis Binks was handed his debut against the Swiss and he too did not look out of place.

However, Luke Graham has yet to make his Scotland debut so could this be an opportunity to blood Stoke City's 22-year-old summer signing?

Aaron Hickey's injury record means the Brentford 24-year-old is not being risked over two matches in one week but he could return after being rested against the Swiss.

Indeed, there was a clamour among the pundits on BBC Radio Scotland's Sportsound for Hickey to be moved to right central defence, ostensibly to make space for flying winger Ben Gannon-Doak.

More of that later, but that would mean Torino's Nathan Patterson dropping out of the right wing-back spot after a difficult night against the talented Swiss forward line.

On the other side of the park, captain Andy Robertson was replaced with Sassuolo's Josh Doig for the final 15 minutes of Tuesday's lost cause but it is unthinkable that the Tottenham Hotspur man will be handed any more rest in Skopje.

That brings us on to the aforementioned Gannon-Doak.

The 20-year-old's frustrations at a lack of starting spots with Bournemouth have continued with Scotland under Pocognoli so far, but he helped the side improve their attacking threat as a substitute after the break in Slovenia.

He then showed his willingness to track back and defend in a backs-to-the-wall second half against the Swiss.

With the visit to Skopje being viewed as a must-win for Scotland's outside chances of finishing top ahead of the Swiss, or even second, Gannon-Doak's speed and trickery are being touted as essential to shoe into the starting line-up.

Josh McPake is a similar option on the other wing, but the Heart of Midlothian 25-year-old is likely to have to wait a tad longer for his debut.

In the continued absence of Scott McTominay, central midfield almost picks itself.

Napoli team-mate Billy Gilmour has been a standout in both games under Pocognoli, while Bologna captain Lewis Ferguson is effective in doing the dirty work in protecting the defence.

If anyone's place is under threat, it could be John McGinn.

While a Scotland mainstay for so many years - and often their biggest goal threat - he has been less influential over the past two games and is perhaps feeling the effects of a heavy schedule at home and in Europe with Aston Villa.

However, there are no standout replacements for that number 10 role, with fellow 31-year-old Ryan Christie having been more effective recently as a defensive midfielder with Bournemouth.

Meanwhile, Udinese 20-year-old Lennon Miller and uncapped Blackburn Rovers 22-year-old Kristi Montgomery have not even featured as substitutes.

Pocognoli could spring a surprise by reverting to the two-winger approach often adopted by predecessor Steve Clarke, which would mean one lone striker, or one withdrawn into a number 10 role.

Oli McBurnie proved effective in that role in the second half against Slovenia but, so far, the Belgian has preferred a two-pronged attack.

McBurnie again impressed against Switzerland before running out of steam in the second half and the Hull City 30-year-old would count himself unlucky not to be handed his third straight start after his recall from the international wilderness.

However, should Pocognoli decide to go with fresh legs, both Sevilla's Robbie Ure and Sassuolo's Kieron Bowie have shown in flashes that they can be a threat at this level.

The latter in particular was unfortunate, having contributed a couple of nice touches before being sacrificed early after Hendry's red card on Tuesday.

Goalkeeper continues to be Scotland's Achilles heel.

With the legendary Craig Gordon approaching an injury-hit end to his career and now retired, Angus Gunn has taken over as the undisputed number one.

However, despite having more regular club starts since his summer move from Nottingham Forest to San Jose Earthquakes, the 30-year-old has received some criticism for Switzerland's first and third goals on Tuesday.

The alternatives, though, are limited. Scott Bain has only four caps and has had his own high-profile slip-ups amid good form with Falkirk this season, while Liam Kelly remains without club game time as second choice with Rangers.

Could Pocognoli take the risk of a change even though North Macedonia are expected to pose a lesser threat than Slovenia or Switzerland?

articles.title: Las consecuencias a las que se expone Cristiano
articles.standfirst: Según el Reglamento de la Federación portuguesa le podrían sancionar durante seis meses y multar económicamente
articles.summary: Según el Reglamento de la Federación portuguesa le podrían sancionar durante seis meses y multar económicamente
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo abandonó la concentración de la selección de Portugal después de la rueda de prensa de Jorge Jesus, en la que el seleccionador defendió su autoridad para decidir las alineaciones. Tras estas palabras del técnico, CR7 puso rumbo a Madrid desde Copenhague en su avión privado. Una decisión que, más allá de que CR7 no regrese al combinado nacional, como apunta O Jogo, puede tener consecuencias para él. Según el Reglamento Disciplinario de la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol (FPF), Cristiano se arriesga a una sanción que puede incluir una suspensión de entre uno y seis meses y una multa económica. "Cualquier jugador que, habiendo sido convocado regularmente, abandone injustificadamente o no se presente a un entrenamiento, un partido o cualquier actividad de las selecciones nacionales o relacionada con la representación deportiva de la FPF o Portugal, será sancionado con una suspensión de uno a seis meses y, adicionalmente, si el jugador es profesional, con una multa de entre 5 y 10 UC [entre aproximadamente 500 y 1.000 euros, siendo 102 euros por unidad de cuenta]", se lee en el reglamento. Además, el párrafo segundo del artículo 160 del Reglamento de la FPF dice lo siguiente: "La ausencia o el abandono conllevan la suspensión preventiva automática del jugador en los términos establecidos en este reglamento", añade el texto. De manera oficial, la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol confirmó el miércoles por la tarde en un comunicado que Cristiano abandonaba la concentración, pero sin explicar los motivos, y aseguró que la preparación de los partidos contra Dinamarca y Noruega continuaría según lo previsto con los otros 24 convocados. "Toda la delegación mantiene el foco absoluto en los próximos compromisos de la selección nacional y en la consecución de los objetivos definidos", señaló el organismo. Cristiano, por su parte, también se pronunció a través de las redes sociales, donde aseguró que más adelante explicará las razones por las que tomó la decisión de marcharse. "Después de la rueda de prensa del entrenador de la selección nacional, y tras una conversación con el presidente de la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol, decidí abandonar el campo de entrenamiento de la Selección. A su debido tiempo contaré la verdad a todos los portugueses sobre las razones que me motivaron a dejar la selección a la que siempre me dediqué. Ahora es el momento de desear buena suerte a Portugal y a todos mis compañeros de equipo, sin excepción", escribió CR7.

articles.title: Klopp zanja los comentarios racistas que acusan a Alemania de "no ser lo suficientemente blanca"
articles.standfirst: "El gran problema de nuestra vida es que todo el mundo puede expresar su opinión"
articles.summary: "El gran problema de nuestra vida es que todo el mundo puede expresar su opinión"
articles.body: Jürgen Klopp, nuevo seleccionador de Alemania, reaccionó con contundencia tras ser preguntado por los comentarios racistas surgigos en redes sociales tras la derrota de 'Die Mannschaft' ante Grecia por 0-1. Algunos usuarios afirmaron que el equipo de Alemania "no era lo suficientemente alemán" o "no lo suficientemente blanco". "No hay motivo para preocuparse por esa gente. No van a ocupar mis pensamientos", dijo el seleccionador alemán en la rueda de prensa previa al partido contra Serbia. Jürgen Klopp, que ha reconocido en diversas ocasiones que no dedica mucho tiempo a las redes sociales, apuntó que "el gran problema de nuestra vida es que todo el mundo puede expresar su opinión. Es una locura que ocurran cosas así". El seleccionador destacó la multiculturalidad del vestuario de la selección de Alemania: "El grupo que tenemos aquí no podría dar un ejemplo mejor de convivencia". "El mundo debería tomar ejemplo de un vestuario deportivo. Allí se respeta a cada uno basándose en hechos reales, y no se le desacredita por opiniones erróneas. ¡Y punto!", sentenció.

articles.title: Inside Northern Ireland's football conveyor belt as Michael O'Neill visits Campbell College
articles.summary: BBC Sport NI spends the day at the IFA JD Academy Residential at Campbell College where Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill catches up with the young players hoping to graduate to a full-time career.
articles.body:
Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill has made no bones about his desire to give youth a chance.

Included in the squad this international window are teenagers Ceadach O'Neill, Tom Atcheson, Braiden Graham and Kieran Morrison, while 21-year-old Patrick Kelly and 22-year-old Terry Devlin have begun to stake their claim for regular inclusion.

A golden generation, or is this simply Northern Ireland's football factory - the IFA JD National Academy - beginning to bear fruit?

As Northern Ireland fans began to digest Monday's 0-0 draw at home to Hungary, following a 1-0 win in Georgia on Friday which has ensured a positive start to their Nations League campaign, O'Neill visited Campbell College which is home to the academy where teenage hopefuls seek to develop into potential stars at club and international level.

"I know about all these players in here, know the clubs they are attracting attention from, their positions," O'Neill told BBC Sport NI.

"We have regular meetings as staff every month with regular updates on the academy and where those players are going.

"Our job is to prepare them as best as possible and guide them if that opportunity comes to take the next step into the professional game in England or Scotland."

Football skills and education of equal importance

The academy at Campbell College is a residential, designed for 24 elite young players at under-15 and under-16 level, providing preparation for life away from home should that come to pass.

While athletes, they remain students with equal emphasis on football and life skills. Education in the classroom is a key component because, in the world of professional football, there are no guarantees.

Academy student Bailey Magee plays at club level with Glenavon.

His day is typical for a 16-year-old with school dominating until mid-afternoon. Once the bell rings, however, it is time to hit the gym and the pitch before returning to any school work in the evening.

If his dream of becoming a professional footballer comes true, then spending so much time away from home will be worth it.

"Going away with Northern Ireland has helped me because I'm able to stay away from home and you get used to that a wee bit," said Magee.

"The hardest times are [after] Christmas because that's when you're coming back after spending a long time with family.

"The IFA and Campbell have done really well when you're trying to mix the two and balance football with studies.

"I'll work hard until the end of the year and whatever happens, happens. I'll maybe do A-Levels, maybe a B.Tech or full-time football academy with the likes of Linfield or Larne, so there are loads of different pathways for us."

Those sentiments are shared by 15-year-old Kayson Braniff who is currently on the books at Linfield.

"My dad had drilled it into my head that we need our studies," he said.

"It's not as if football is everything, studies come first because you definitely need them in case football doesn't work out."

Investing in youth paying dividends - O'Neill

Clubs in England have the ability to integrate young players into their systems from a young age, which can mean those from NI playing catch-up if and when they make the switch in their mid-teens.

Therefore, preparing potential stars for the rigours of life in a new environment with new coaches can only be enhanced by time in the NI academy which O'Neill believes makes teenagers "better equipped" to make their mark at an English or Scottish club.

Helping young players realise their professional dream is intrinsic, but for Northern Ireland, unearthing new stars to graduate into the senior team is equally important.

"Two or three years ago we brought players in a bit younger than their club career suggested they were at that level, but it pays dividends now," said the current boss.

"You need the right people in the right positions to make that work and I think we have that.

"Players have decisions to make on their club situations and international situations, but your pathway is very important as it builds a loyalty within players.

"We want young players from whatever part of the community they come from to be part of this pathway to become senior international players."

Pathways are all well and good, but watching previous graduates from the academy go on to wear the green jersey or star in Champions League games like Conor Bradley ensures it is a tangible goal for those currently involved.

The current Northern Ireland manager taking such an active interest helps too.

"He's a really nice guy and to think I could be in that team in the next few years, which is the goal, it's really reassuring," Magee said of his sitdown with O'Neill on Tuesday.

Braniff agreed O'Neill's interest confirms "he cares about the youth".

Both are hopeful they can follow in the footsteps of previous graduates. If that results in a move to a full-time club, it will represent another success story for the academy.

"It doesn't matter who it's for or where it is, so long as it's a professional team and a professional contract," said Braniff.

Watch our full behind the scenes access , external on the BBC NI YouTube channel right now.

articles.title: Republic of Ireland v Austria: We will learn from mistakes made - Hallgrimsson
articles.summary: Republif of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson says he and the Football Association of Ireland can learn from mistakes around the build-up to Sunday's Israel game as they prepare to face Austria tonight.
articles.body:
Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson cut an almost frustrated figure after fielding questions before Thursday's Nations League Group B3 game against Austria at Dublin's Aviva Stadium (19:45 BST).

The conversation would normally revolve around the opposition or his own team's preparation, but this has been no ordinary international window with the fall-out from Sunday's 3-0 win over Israel , plus the chaotic build-up to that game in Debrecen still dominating discourse.

On Saturday, players voted to fulfil the Israel fixtures following goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu's decision to make himself unavailable, with the issue continuing to hang over the Irish camp before Sunday's behind-closed-doors return in Serbia.

Protests have continued this week with the 'Stop The Game' campaign - organised by the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine - issuing an open letter calling for a boycott of this Sunday's game in Backa Topola due to the Israel-Gaza war.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) has come under fire for their handling of the saga, with board members appearing before the Oireachtas (Irish parliament) Sports Committee in Dublin on Wednesday , while Hallgrimsson reflected on a "challenging time for me as a leader".

"I would think the Association would learn from these events like I will learn from them," the Republic of Ireland boss said on Wednesday.

"I think we will all look back and be better afterwards, the same for the FAI. Probably, they will look back and think 'we should have done this or said this' but in real time, you tend to make some wrong decisions.

"We would like to look forward and we are in a pre-match press conference before a game against Austria and we haven't spoken about football."

Former Republic of Ireland manager Brian Kerr has been consistent in his calls for a boycott of the Israel games.

Speaking on Virgin Media on Saturday, he said Bazunu was "feeling quite low and shunned by some of the players and by the FAI", and was not included in the players' vote that FAI CEO David Courell said passed by a "significant majority" in favour of fulfilling the Israel fixtures.

Hallgrimsson would not be drawn on Kerr's comments, insisting he had not read or listened to them fully and suggested social media was a factor for the rising temperature before the Israel games.

"I know he [Kerr] has been vocal and has a strong opinion, but I don't read the news and I don't be on social media, so I wouldn't be able to quote on that one," he said.

"Like I've said, [people have] strong opinions and when you have a strong opinion, you have to be able to listen to others.

"It is easy to get carried away with social media but in the end, time will be our judge. Sometimes you are under pressure from social media to take a stand instead of thinking deeper."

Last week, the Israel Football Association accused Hallgrimsson of "ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity" after the coach said, "we're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide".

The armed Palestinian group Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023, killing about 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages.

In response, Israel launched a massive military offensive in Gaza, during which more than 73,000 people have been killed, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

Israel has repeatedly denied that it has committed genocide, as well as war crimes and crimes against humanity. It says its military operations in Gaza have been conducted in self-defence and in accordance with international law.

"It's one thing to have a personal opinion and then it's another thing to be the leader of a group," he continued.

"We need to take everything into consideration when we pick a team, when we talk about a squad, talk about subjects.

"I have been drawn into a political venue and I'm not an expert in politics, so this is learning for me, learning as a coach, learning as a leader and as a human being.

"There is a lot we have gone through when we will reflect on when all of this is finished and that is why I'm trying to focus on football now as that's my job. Then I can reflect on how I am as a human being and a leader."

articles.title: Flick no repetirá el mismo error con Raphinha y ya hace cábalas para suplirle en la delantera
articles.standfirst: El técnico no olvida que forzó el regreso del brasileño el curso pasado y recayó
articles.summary: El técnico no olvida que forzó el regreso del brasileño el curso pasado y recayó
articles.body: Hansi Flick no correrá riesgos en el regreso de Raphinha, que fue desconvocado ayer miércoles con Brasil a causa de un edema en la parte posterior del muslo derecho. El técnico alemán aún no ha olvidado, ni superado, que el curso pasado, en octubre, forzó su regreso al trabajo y el internacional brasileño recayó de su dolencia, que era, además, en la misma zona que ahora tiene dañada. El preparador, de hecho, ya hace cávalas para encontrar un sustituto al exprofesional del Leeds, que llegará en las próximas horas a Barcelona y se someterá a pruebas, por si no ve claro su retorno para el encuentro contra el Getafe del sábado día 10. Flick reconoció como error propio la recaída de Raphinha de sus molestias en el muslo, concretamente en el bíceps femoral, el curso pasado. El preparador admitió, públicamente, que minimizó la dolencia y que gestionó mal los plazos de su reincorporación, y eso provocó que tuviera que alargar casi un mes más su baja. Entre los muchos partidos que se perdió, destaca el Clásico. Ahora, el partido contra el Real Madrid vuelve a estar en el horizonte: se juega el domingo 25 en el Spotify Camp Nou. El germano no quiere que la historia se repita e irá con pies de plomo con la vuelta del brasileño, que será sometido, en cuanto aterrice en las próximas horas a Barcelona desde Australia, a nuevas pruebas para comprobar, con los profesionales culés, el alcance de las molestias en la parte posterior del muslo derecho, tiene un edema, que forzaron su cambio en el descanso del partido amistoso de Brasil del pasado martes. Flick impondrá, por lo tanto, máxima prudencia en el regreso de Raphinha y de ahí que esté ya meditando las opciones que tiene para relevarle en la punta del ataque culé para el encuentro contra el Getafe del próximo sábado día 10. El exprofesional del Leeds no está, no obstante, aún descartado para este compromiso, dependerá de los resultados de las pruebas a las que se someta en las próximas horas y de su evolución. Las posibilidades para suplirle, en caso de que el brasileño no se recupere a tiempo, son variadas y los jugadores a los que puede recurrir tienen perfiles y registros bien distintos. Los recambios más naturales son Gabriel Jesus y el joven Hamza Abdelkarim, delanteros centros natos. Aunque los dos fichajes de esta temporada apenas han intervenido. El brasileño suma 41 minutos repartidos en cuatro encuentros, aunque ha firmado ya dos goles. Y el egipcio únicamente ha jugado 4' con la camiseta azulgrana: fue en el encuentro de LaLiga contra el Rayo. Pero también han tenido minutos y han rendido con suficiencia en la posición de falso 9: Dani Olmo, Fermín López, Anthony Gordon y Karim Adeyemi. Tampoco está descartado Lamine Yamal para la plaza de delantero centro, pero es menos probable. Flick tiene muchas opciones tiene, aunque la baja de Raphinha sería muy sensible para el Barça: el capitán suma 14 goles este curso.

articles.title: La inmunidad del 'jefe' del City podría complicar las acciones legales por las trampas de su equipo
articles.standfirst: El estatus de Khaldoon al-Mubarak lo protege en Gran Bretaña de un procesamiento penal
articles.summary: El estatus de Khaldoon al-Mubarak lo protege en Gran Bretaña de un procesamiento penal
articles.body: El 'Financial Times' informa que Khaldoon al-Mubarak, presidente emiratí del Manchester City, obtuvo la inmunidad diplomática hace seis años. Esa medida "podría complicar cualquier acción legal derivada de los hallazgos de que Manchester City infló artificialmente sus finanzas en más de 1.000 millones de euros". El estatus de Khaldoon al-Mubarak lo protege en Gran Bretaña de un procesamiento penal y, en la mayoría de los casos, de procedimientos civiles. Los hallazgos de la Comisión podrían tensar las relaciones entre el Reino Unido y los Emiratos Árabes Unidos, ya que Khaldoon Al Mubarak supervisa una sociedad de inversión soberana que ha generado 35.129 millones de euros en compromisos de inversión de los Emiratos hacia Gran Bretaña. Los abogados dicen que la inmunidad diplomática de Khaldoon Al Mubarak podría complicar mucho cualquier intento de demandarlo personalmente en los tribunales del Reino Unido después del caso del Manchester City. La aerolínea de Emiratos Árabes Unidos, Etihad, uno de los principales patrocinadores del Manchester City, ha negado los cargos de los que se ha culpado al club inglés y sopesa tomar medidas legales contra la Premier League. La Premier League afirma que el Manchester City concertó "contratos ficticios (que tergiversaban el acuerdo real entre las partes) con varios de sus socios comerciales, además de recurrir a acuerdos "ficticios" con otros, para inflar artificialmente los ingresos del club y reducir sus costes". También acusa al City de alterar falsamente su situación financiera por un valor de más de 1.050 millones de euros. El club había pactado acuerdos de patrocinio desorbitados con diversas empresas, pero dichos patrocinadores solo abonaban una parte de la cifra acordada. El resto era cubierto por Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), propietaria del club. Tal y como señala la Premier League, esto permitió al City "inflar artificialmente los ingresos del club" y, por consiguiente, gastar más conforme a la normativa de la competición.

articles.title: Radu colidera la clasificación del Trofeo Zamora
articles.standfirst: Con Sivera es el portero menos batido hasta la fecha
articles.summary: Con Sivera es el portero menos batido hasta la fecha
articles.body: Además de jugarlo todo, Radu echa el candado a la portería del Celta. El meta rumano es, junto a Sivera, el portero menos batido de LaLiga. Ha encajado 6 goles en las 7 primeras jornadas, a una media de 0’86 por partido. El céltico comparte el primer puesto del Trofeo Zamora, que Marca concede al portero menos batido de la competición. Además, Radu ya ha dejado tres porterías a cero en el arranque de campeonato, algo que la pasada temporada no consiguió hasta la 13ª jornada. El pasado año, en su debut en LaLiga, encajó 48 goles en los 38 partidos, ya que no se perdió ni un minuto de la competición. La media fue de 1’26 goles encajados por partido, media que en el arranque de esta temporada rebaja en 0’40. Radu, que estos días se encuentra con la selección rumana, lo juega todo con Claudio Giráldez. En poco más de un año no se perdido ni un partido de Liga y en total suma ya 58 partidos oficiales con el Celta. La llegada de Bayindir, procedente del Manchester United este verano, no ha impedido que lo haya jugado todo también en el inicio de esta temporada.

articles.title: Man City charges: Premier League executives would be 'staggered' if clubs vote for expulsion as punishment
articles.summary: Sky Sports News understands that discussions remain ongoing within, and between, the bosses of other clubs in the Premier League about how they might react to developments in the Man City case; City's commercial appeal is seen as playing a key role in the attraction of the Premier League
articles.body:
Expulsion is one of several punishments available to the independent commission, which earlier this week found Man City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them over alleged financial mismanagement. Other potential sanctions include a fine, a points deduction and/or a transfer embargo.

Man City remain adamant they are innocent and have vowed to fight the judgement.

Sky Sports News has been told discussions remain ongoing within, and between, the bosses of other clubs in the Premier League about how they might react to developments, with a number of them considering their own legal positions in terms of a possible financial claim against Man City.

But in a new and surprising development, we have been told that many rival clubs consider Man City such a key part of the commercial attraction of the Premier League, both in the UK and globally, that if rival clubs voted to expel them, it would be as if those clubs were "cutting off their noses to spite their faces".

"If Man City were expelled, that would have massive commercial consequences for everyone in the league, and ultimately it would cost the other clubs an awful lot of money," one executive, who didn't want to be named, told Sky Sports News .

He went on to explain that, should such a decision come during this or next season, it would mean only 19 clubs playing the remaining fixtures, with broadcasters in the UK and abroad likely to seek refunds due to the reduction in the number and attractiveness of the games they had paid to televise.

Sponsorship and other corporate sources of funding might well be reduced across the board if the most dominant club in English football in the last two decades were no longer playing in the Premier League.

Similarly, expulsion would bring the futures of stars like Erling Haaland, Phil Foden and more into question, which would further risk the commercial attractiveness of the Premier League and, according to one source, would make expulsion "a risk not worth taking".

A further issue could be the uncertainty created by top clubs deciding to go against the recommended sanction laid out by the independent commission.

It's thought there is a counter-feeling among some top clubs that Manchester City remaining in the Premier League would be damaging to the brand and integrity of the competition, and that an extended period outside the top flight for City, even though it would lead to short-term financial pain, is necessary to maintain the league's global image for the future.

The differences of opinion within Premier League clubs will not affect the independent commission's decision, but it could be a factor if the clubs are forced to vote on City's possible expulsion.

If that commission were to recommend City be expelled, and then the Premier League clubs voted against such a move, it is unprecedented and unknown what - if any - punishment could then be brought against City.

Championship directors averse to Man City joining league

Latest from Sky Sports News' Lyall Thomas and Anthony Joseph:

Sky Sports News has sought out some of the current sentiment in the Championship about Man City potentially joining their league.

If there was an expulsion from the Premier League, Man City's future would then reside in the hands of the FA and EFL. A vote would have to take place involving all 72 clubs and a majority decision would be needed to determine where - and if - they enter into the EFL.

However, another possibility is a points deduction and one that could be severe enough to see Man City relegated to the Championship.

One top Championship club director believes Man City dropping into the Championship has "absolutely no" benefit for the league whatsoever and would prevent another club being promoted.

They said: "What benefit has the Championship got with Man City dropping into it? Absolutely none.

"The finances are so big they'll just blow the Championship away and go straight back up. So it kills a promotion spot for the other clubs. There isn't another club in the Championship that could handle that level of wealth."

Another Championship director told Sky Sports News : "Whoever is making the decision on any sanctions has to uphold the integrity of the whole English football pyramid - and not only be thinking of the Premier League.

"It shouldn't be the case that if they are expelled from the Premier League that they can just join the Championship. That should be for us to decide. They should have to earn their way back up English football."

Another Championship club source said: "It's not for us to comment on this process. There is a lot of uncertainty and speculation at the moment. But really no-one knows what's going to happen. I just hope that our [EFL clubs'] interests are considered and treated fairly."

articles.title: Scaloni siente la ausencia de Messi: "Con él la cosa cambia"
articles.standfirst: "Es irremplazable, pero buscaremos la manera de jugar igual, a través de la pelota, juntar pases y llegar al arco. Esa es la identidad de esta selección", asegura el técnico
articles.summary: "Es irremplazable, pero buscaremos la manera de jugar igual, a través de la pelota, juntar pases y llegar al arco. Esa es la identidad de esta selección", asegura el técnico
articles.body: Antes del encuentro contra Benín que significará la despedida de Messi de la selección y un homenaje para el 10, Argentina se impuso con claridad a Bolivia (4-0) en un amistoso disputado en el Estadio Mario Kempes, el primer partido desde la final del Mundial que perdió contra España La selección de Argentina afronta una nueva etapa ya sin la presencia de Messi, anunció su retirada del combinado nacional. Una ausencia a la que se refirió el seleccionador Scaloni tras el encuentro. "Messi es irremplazable, pero buscaremos la manera de jugar igual, con el mismo sentido, a través de la pelota, juntar pases y llegar al arco. Creo que esa es la identidad de esta selección, más allá de quién esté, aunque con él la cosa cambia. El desafío es seguir jugando de esta manera, y que los chicos que vengan entiendan que esa es la forma", afirmó Scaloni. Sobre el encuentro ante Bolivia, el seleccionador comentó: “La sensación es que los futbolistas afrontaron el partido como tiene que ser cada vez que se viste esta camiseta. Más allá del resultado, se vio que el equipo tiene una identidad y juegue quien juegue se va a respetar. Individualmente es difícil después de una victoria así, todo el equipo hizo un partido completo. Todos vienen con ganas, demuestran que quieren estar. No hay otra manera de afrontar los partidos”. En cuanto a quién será el heredero del dorsal 10 que portaba Messi, Scaloni no dio muchas pistas. "Hasta el día 6 la va a usar Leo y, a partir de la siguiente fecha, veremos a quién se la damos. Hay un montón que la pueden llevar, antes de oficializarse lo va a saber el jugador”, aseguró.

articles.title: Cristiano, reincidente: "Fui a explicarle que no iba a jugar y lo malinterpretó"
articles.standfirst: Así lo recuerda Fernando Santos, el que fuera seleccionador de Portugal en el Mundial de 2022
articles.summary: Así lo recuerda Fernando Santos, el que fuera seleccionador de Portugal en el Mundial de 2022
articles.body: La crisis que se vive en Portugal con Cristiano Ronaldo no es nueva. El jugador lleva mal no jugar defendiendo los colores de su país y es por eso que ha abandonado la concentración esta semana. Pero la situación no es nueva. Todo esto ya se vivió en el Mundial de 2022. Así lo recuerda Fernando Santos, el que fuera seleccionador luso en aquella cita mundialista. En una entrevista concedida a A Bola en 2023, el técnico comentaba que a él le pasó lo mismo: "Fui a explicarle que no iba a jugar y lo malinterpretó". Al parecer, el entrenador le llamó a su despacho el mismo día de partido y, tras la comida, le explicó la situación. Por lo visto, Cristiano no entendió la situación y se lo tomó muy mal. No abandonó la concentración, pero su relación con Santos ya nunca volvería a ser la misma. "No hemos hablado desde el día que llegué de Qatar. Cristiano sabe que, el día que suena el teléfono, siempre estoy aquí", asegura el entrenador.

articles.title: Drogheda United set to face Mohammed Salah's Trabzonspor
articles.summary: Drogheda United will travel to Turkey to face Trabzonspor at the 40,000-seat Papara Park as part of a special relationship between the two clubs.
articles.body:
In August, Mohamed Salah was given a hero's welcome as he was unveiled to Trabzonspor fans at a packed 40,000-seat Papara Park.

That same weekend, Drogheda United travelled to Galway to play out a 0-0 draw in a League of Ireland tie in front of 5,000 fans.

Yet on Thursday, the two will meet in a friendly on the Black Sea coast in north east Turkey as part of a two-decade-long connection between the clubs.

"In 2006, in a Trabzonspor forum online, a couple of fans realised that there was a small Irish club that had the star and crescent, which are obviously symbols from the Turkish flag," Drogheda chief executive Rian Wogan tells BBC Sport.

"From there they then subsequently realised that our club colours are also claret and blue and messages started going back and forward."

The wider relationship between Ireland and Turkey goes back even further, forged during the 1800s.

The Ottoman Empire provided humanitarian aid to Ireland during the Great Famine, with the Ottoman Sultan donating £1,000.

The two countries also celebrate 75 years of diplomatic relations this year.

In 2008, Drogheda went into examinership, Ireland's equivalent of administration, and were deducted 10 points in the league.

Trabzonspor fans heard of their plight and sent letters to the club with cash inside.

Two years later, their relationship was made official when they became sister clubs and there were plans for a ceremonial friendly in Dublin in 2013.

"They travelled over here to play and there was a freak deluge of rain that fell within an hour of kick-off," explains Wogan.

"We had our staff in the turnstiles waiting to scan tickets in, but the game was deemed unplayable and Trabzonspor went home without playing the fixture."

So Thursday's match has been a long time coming.

When Drogheda announced the friendly on social media on 2 September, Trabzonspor fans reacted in their droves. The post on X has been seen well over half a million times.

About 30% of Drogheda's social media following is from Turkey. More than their share of followers from Ireland.

And it is not just online where the crossover of fans is being seen.

Trabzonspor shirts and flags are commonly spotted at Drogheda matches and Turkish fans sometimes visit the club during the week just to see the stadium.

One Trabzonspor fan, Cafer Bektas, lives a couple of miles outside Drogheda and attends every game.

When he first moved to the area, wearing a Trabzonspor jersey caught the attention of locals and got him discounts in shops.

Drogheda fans will be hoping for similar treatment when they make the 4,700km trip to Turkey, a journey between 30 and 35 Boynesiders fans are set to make.

Some Trabzonspor fans have already offered their homes to visiting supporters.

Whether or not they will get to witness Salah face their club remains to be seen.

He was left out of Egypt's squad that faced South Sudan in an Africa Cup of Nations qualifier on Tuesday due to the match being played on artificial turf.

Wogan thinks even his presence would add to the weight of the game.

"He might not be in the squad, but even to have him in the stadium would be incredible," he says.

"Trabzonspor have done amazing business in the last couple of windows and have really pushed the boundaries. The prospect of facing them is incredible."

Salah or no Salah, the two clubs will be marking a special and unlikely relationship.

articles.title: El griego Vassillis Foitas pita el España-República Checa
articles.standfirst: Es su primer partido con ambas selecciones
articles.summary: Es su primer partido con ambas selecciones
articles.body: España y la República Checa ya conocen el nombre del árbitro del partido que las enfrenta este sábado en el Carlos Tartiere a partir de las 20.45 horas. La UEFA ha designado al griego Vassillis Foitas. Es la primera vez que pita a España. Tampoco ha dirigido a equipos españoles en competiciones europeas. Sí fue el árbitro del amistoso sub 21 que España perdió 3-1 en marzo de 2025, el de los tres goles de Woltemade. Santi Denia era el entrenador español. El 28 de julio de 2024 dirigió la final del Sub 19, la que España ganó 2-0 a Francia en Windsor Park. También es su primer partido con los checos. Natural de Pellas (10-4-1989) es un árbitro de corto recorrido internacional. Hizo su debut en la primera división griega, , el 20 de octubre de 2018, arbitrando el partido PAS Giannina - Panaitōlikos (0-2). Fue ascendido a la categoría internacional en 2021 y se estrenó como árbitro de la UEFA en el partido de la primera ronda de clasificación de la UEFA Conference League entre Sfîntul Gheorghe y Partizani Tirana (2-3). Camino del Mundial pasado, estuvo a los mandos del Azerbaiyán 1-Ucrania 1. Y en la Liga de las Naciones pasada pitó el Alemania 7 - Bosnia Herzegovina 0.

articles.title: Asencio, operado con éxito
articles.standfirst: El central ha sido intervenido por el doctor Manuel Leyes de una fractura en la tibia de la pierna derecha y estará cerca de cuatro meses de baja
articles.summary: El central ha sido intervenido por el doctor Manuel Leyes de una fractura en la tibia de la pierna derecha y estará cerca de cuatro meses de baja
articles.body: Raúl Asencio ha sido operado con éxito por el prestigioso traumatólogo Manuel Leyes en el Centro Olympia de Madrid. El defensa se ha sometido a una intervención quirúrgica para corregir una fractura por estrés en la tibia de la pierna derecha, lesión que arrastraba desde el pasado mes de enero y que tras la última recaída esta misma semana le ha obligado a pasar por el quirófano. La intervención se ha realizado de forma satisfactoria y ahora el central afronta una recuperación que estará en torno a los cuatro meses de baja. Tras la intervención, recibió la visita de su entrenador, Jose Mourinho. Asencio era uno de los pocos jugadores que estaban disponibles para Jose Mourinho en Valdebebas por las bajas por el parón internacional. El central aún no ha debutado con el Real Madrid esta temporada en partido oficial. El 30 de julio, sufrió una lesión muscular en el recto femoral de la pierna derecha que lo mantuvo fuera de las convocatorias hasta el 12 de septiembre, para el partido contra el Rayo Vallecano. Posteriormente, ha estado en el banquillo en los tres últimos compromisos del equipo blanco, pero no ha disfrutado de minutos. Y ahora afrontará un tiempo de recuperación que rondará los cuatro meses. Un nuevo episodio de dolor en la zona dañada, en la tibia de la pierna derecha, fue el detonante definitivo para que se tomara la decisión de que el jugador fuera intervenido quirúrgicamente. La operación llevaba rondando a Asencio desde el final de la temporada pasada, cuando ya estuvo sobre la mesa esa opción, aprovechando el verano para amortiguar el largo tiempo de baja. El club ha emitido después un comunicado sobre la intervención del central: "Nuestro jugador Raúl Asencio ha sido intervenido hoy con éxito por el doctor Manuel Leyes de una fractura por estrés en la tibia derecha. La operación ha sido supervisada por los Servicios Médicos del Real Madrid. Asencio comenzará en los próximos días su proceso de recuperación".
