articles.title: Scotland: Findlay Curtis shines as revamped youth set up begins
articles.summary: Amidst a raft of coaching changes in Scotland's youth set up, the under-21s delivered an eye-catching display, with Rangers winger Findlay Curtis at the heart of it.
articles.body:
As starts to a new era go, Scotland Under-21s' dominant 5-2 defeat of Azerbaijan was a rousing one.

Findlay Curtis ran riot, Tyler Fletcher cruised through the game in midfield and three strikers all scored.

All of that contributed to a fantastic team performance full of attacking elan and aggressive pressing.

It was exactly the type of display new head coach Tony Docherty and his assistant Steven Naismith demanded after replacing Scot Gemmill, who had been in charge of Scotland's best young talent for the past decade.

Those appointments were the headline amid a sweeping set of changes to the coaching set-up across Scotland's international youth teams initiated by the Scottish FA's new chief football officer Craig Mulholland.

The aim is to create a more streamlined and effective pathway for Scotland youth players into Sebastien Pocognoli's senior men's side.

It may only be one game - and one they should expect to win - but the under-21s certainly showed their intent to emulate the first team.

"My message to them was I want you to create an identity for the Scotland Under-21 team - by your attacking style of play, by your counter-pressing," Docherty told BBC Scotland after his side's win.

"And I thought we did that in abundance. The performance level, enthusiasm and energy of the players was outstanding."

Five-star Scotland Under-21s sweep aside Azerbaijan

Will Pocognoli change goalkeeper after Swiss loss?

The SFA's plan is for the under-21s to reflect the style and structure of the first team, to make it easier for players to move up to the next level.

Docherty was in La Manga at the senior side's training camp before their Nations League games and Pocognoli has given a presentation on his game model to the age-grade coaches.

Mulholland as well as SFA chief executive Ian Maxwell and Scotland assistant Alan Irvine were in Kilmarnock on Wednesday night to observe as Docherty set his team up in the same 3-4-2-1 system Pocognoli favours - and that he himself used at Dundee.

Fletcher and St Mirren's Ryan Carr occupied the midfield berths, with Curtis and James Wilson playing as inside forwards behind West Brom's Barney Stewart.

Scotland pressed high, smothered their opponents and played the ball about quickly and with purpose. It was the type of football Pocognoli described when taking over the Scotland job but that his own team has only delivered in one half against Slovenia so far.

"They want us to mirror exactly what the first team do," former Falkirk striker Stewart, who scored twice on the night, told BBC Scotland.

"We sit down and watch the first-team games. I've got everyone in my ear saying, 'you see what they did there?' We watch patterns of play, pressing, you name it."

In that same vein, Curtis and Wilson joined up with the under-21s, having initially been involved in the senior squad's camp. It could have been viewed as a setback for them and Fletcher too, the trio having already played for the men's side.

However, none of them showed it on the pitch, as Curtis had a hand in all five of the goals, with Fletcher and Wilson both scoring.

"I came back with them from the camp," Docherty said. "They couldn't have been better with their attitude and leadership in the group.

"The team performance, including the subs, was really strong. But they deserve special mention because their attitude to the group has been brilliant and we need to make sure we continue that going forward."

The revamp of Scotland's youth teams at national level spreads well beyond the under-21s.

Docherty and Naismith are only two of a suite of new coaches, starting as low as the new under-14s squad.

Former Dundee United manager Tam Courts is leading the under-19s programme alongside former Hearts and Rangers left-back Lee Wallace, who is back at Tynecastle as a youth coach.

Courts managed to steer United into fourth in the Scottish Premiership in 2022 with a young squad, before departing for a short stint at Honved in Hungary.

David McCallum, who led the Rangers and Queen's Park academy, is paired with former Aberdeen and Celtic winger Jonny Hayes, now a coach with the latter, at under-17 level.

While at under-16s, Rhys McCabe is in charge, after his successful spell as a player- manager at Airdrieonians, alongside current SFA coaches James Grady and Stephen Clarke.

They will all be helped by former Aberdeen first team coach Peter Leven and Neil McFarlane, who works as Brentford's first-team coach, having led their B-side before that.

The idea is that while each group has been given an age grade to work with, they will operate more as a team so everyone has eyes across the entire pathway.

To help with that process, the coaches will be tasked with introducing a 'Scottish DNA'. So while the under-21s mirror the first team, the age groups below will have more license to play differently from Pocognoli's side, but underpinned by the same principles.

Courts says that will be about channelling the Scottish reputation for passion and hard work - but marrying it with technical improvement.

"If you want to be a team that has credibility on the top stage, for sure we need to have more dominance and control of the ball," he said.

"We need to develop more players that are technically capable of playing in smaller spaces and also creating and scoring chances, because just now at the top level of the game, spaces are at a premium, chances are at a premium and we have to recognise that this is where the game is going.

"We have to develop players that can actually execute in those situations."

It is also no coincidence that the coaches chosen all have significant experience coaching and managing within Scotland's biggest clubs, as the SFA tries to align more with the people who ultimately have a greater hand in the progress of young players on a daily basis.

That is in contrast to Gemmill, as an example, who did not play or coach at a Scottish club and so did not have a natural link.

And while player development is the key focus, the new set-up also creates opportunities and a potential pathway for young coaches like McCabe.

After being thrown into management at just 29 while still playing for Airdrieonians, McCabe managed to make a success of it, leading them from League 1 into the Championship play-offs while playing a possession-based game.

"There's a lot of learning and personal development that I want to do first hand," McCabe said.

"Working with Sebastien and guys that have been about the game at different levels and had different experiences. I want to channel that and use that to ultimately make me a better coach."

The success of these, and other SFA changes to youth football in Scotland, can only ultimately be judged over the long term. But one thing is for sure, they are shaking up the status quo.

articles.title: Valentín Gómez y un soñado debut con Argentina para seguir creciendo
articles.standfirst: El valor del central zurdo en el mercado, pese a no ser titular fijo en el Betis, no para de crecer
articles.summary: El valor del central zurdo en el mercado, pese a no ser titular fijo en el Betis, no para de crecer
articles.body: Valentín Gómez cumplió anoche uno de sus sueños de niño. El central del Betis debutó con la selección absoluta de Argentina, disputando los últimos minutos del partido que el combinado dirigido por Scaloni disputó ante Bolivia (4-0). Sustituyendo a Lisandro Martínez, el zaguero de San Miguel se estrenó como internacional y dio un paso más en su constante crecimiento tanto deportivo como también en el mercado. El conjunto verdiblanco apostó por Valentín el verano de 2025 pagando a Vélez Sarsfield un traspaso de algo más de cinco millones de euros por su pase. Poco más de un año después, el valor del central zurdo, de 23 años de edad, alcanza ya los 12 millones de euros, más del doble de lo que el Betis invirtió. Un salto importante para un jugador que, pese a no ser titular indiscutible con Pellegrini, sí se ha convertido en una pieza muy importante en las rotaciones, aprovechando también una polivalencia que le permite jugar en distintas posiciones. La pasada temporada, la de su estreno en el fútbol europeo, Valentín participó en 41 partidos oficiales entre Liga, Copa del Rey y UEFA Europa League, superando los 2.850 minutos sobre el terreno de juego. Casi la mitad de sus partidos como titular fueron en el puesto de lateral izquierdo, aprovechando la importante carencia que tenían los verdiblancos en esa zona del campo hasta la llegada de Fran García este verano. Ahora, ya ubicado en su posición natural, como central zurdo, sigue sumando. En lo que va de curso, Valentín ha tenido minutos en cuatro de los ocho partidos disputados por su equipo y ha cumplido otro sueño: jugar la Champions League. Tuvo media hora en la victoria de su equipo frente al Lille, en Francia, en la primera jornada de la fase de liga del torneo continental. Ahora le ha llegado la oportunidad de demostrar ante Scaloni que puede ser una pieza útil en el futuro de la albiceleste, que se enfrenta a un importante cambio generacional tras varios años de éxitos de la mano de Leo Messi, que se despide la próxima semana. En el Betis disfrutan del buen momento de Valentín, cada vez más asentado en el equipo y con mejor interpretación sobre el césped de lo que quiere Pellegrini, y valoran positivamente el crecimiento de su valor de mercado. Tratándose de un futbolista joven, con mucho recorrido aún por delante, el central argentino está llamado a ser no solo un recurso importante a nivel deportivo sino, en el futuro, una opción para generar las necesarias plusvalías que permitan al club seguir creciendo.

articles.title: Rafael Leao hereda el mítico '7' de Cristiano Ronaldo
articles.standfirst: El extremo, el elegido para portar el dorsal de CR7
articles.summary: El extremo, el elegido para portar el dorsal de CR7
articles.body: Portugal pasa página tras la espantada histórica de Cristiano Ronaldo. Y es que la UEFA ya ha hecho oficial los nuevos dorsales del equipo luso en los que ya no aparece Cristiano Ronaldo. El mítico '7' pasa a manos de Rafael Leao. El actual jugador del Galatasaray ha sido el elegido para llevar a su espalda el dorsal que será recordado para siempre como el de Cristiano Ronaldo. Es necesario aclarar que la UEFA no permite dejar vacío ningún dorsal por lo que la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol se ha visto obligada a elegir entre uno de sus futbolistas tras el adiós de su gran estrella. Existía la duda sobre el heredero del '7'. João Félix, joven y en un gran momento de forma, también aspiraba a cambiar su actual dorsal '11' por el de su gran ídolo, pero finalmente el elegido ha sido Leao. Ahora, la responsabilidad es para un Rafa Leao que intentará estar a la altura del peso de la historia del número. El extremo portugués de 27 años ha disputado 50 partidos con la elástica lusa en los que ha marcado 6 goles y ha repartido 8 asistencias. articles.title: En el centro del problema
articles.standfirst: A Mou sólo le queda la pieza de Pitarch por probar en un doble pivote que no carbura
articles.summary: A Mou sólo le queda la pieza de Pitarch por probar en un doble pivote que no carbura
articles.body: En la máquina del Real Madrid hay dos piezas que no terminan de funcionar. El doble pivote está en el ojo del huracán por la falta de fútbol del equipo y Mourinho no termina de dar con la tecla. El equipo pedía a gritos en el mercado un recambio que finalmente no llegó de fuera. Sólo Bernardo Silva por Ceballos, un perfil el del portugués más próximo al de Bellingham y Güler que de organizador. Rodri, Vitinha y Zubimendi estuvieron en el escaparate, pero el Madrid no dio el paso. El perfil de jugador que se consideraba más necesario fue el que no llegó. Ahora le toca a Mou trabajar en una solución que no acaba de encontrar. La pareja del centro del campo está siendo un quebradero de cabeza. El técnico sólo parece tener claro que Valverde es intocable. El resto ha sido un baile de jugadores para acompañar al uruguayo sin una conclusión clara: Bernardo Silva, Camavinga, Tchouaméni, Trent... Sólo le queda la opción de Thiago Pitarch por probar. Cuatro parejas distintas en el doble pivote en ocho partidos y siete centros del campo diferentes. Así es el viaje al centro del problema de Mourinho. Porque Bellingham y Güler se salen de la ecuación del doble pivote. A ellos les afecta, pero su responsabilidad está más arriba. Al menos, hasta el momento. Intocable. Ha sido titular en los ocho partidos. Sus socios en el doble pivote han cambiado, pero él siempre ha permanecido en el once inicial. Aun así, el uruguayo no escapa al runrún de su rendimiento en una posición en la que no puede lucir las virtudes que lo llevaron al estrellato: imparables conducciones al espacio, incansable recorrido por banda y un descomunal disparo. Todo eso lo explotaba desde la banda, desde una posición más de interior. Centrado como ahora, se le cuestiona su habilidad para la organización y distribución del juego del equipo. Si se recupera de la lesión sufrida en el derbi, no parece haber ninguna duda de que se mantendrá en el once ante el Villarreal... y en el doble pivote. Tardó en llegar a la temporada por culpa de una lesión. Se ha subido al tren en marcha y le va a costar coger velocidad de crucero. No entró en el primer plan de Zidane para la selección francesa, lo que le hubiese venido bien para acumular minutos. Su papel es el que es y no es precisamente un organizador. Si no tiene a alguien que le ayude en la salida del balón, se le ven más sus dificultades para organizar el juego. Es un jugador con una descomunal fortaleza defensiva, pero organizar y distribuir el juego no es su fuerte. Por ello, la mezcla con Valverde se antoja complicada porque ninguno de los dos es un especialista en la creación. Estuvo en el mercado todo el verano porque la sensación que había era de fin de ciclo. La temporada pasada, en la que fue adelantado por la derecha por el canterano Thiago Pitarch, fue decisiva para que el club se plantease la opción de abrirle la puerta si llegaba una buena oferta. Una idea que no compartía el jugador, que con la llegada de un nuevo entrenador quería intentar volver a ser importante. Mou aceptó el reto de Camavinga, pero la situación del francés apenas ha cambiado por más que el técnico le haya dado cariño en alguna ocasión. "Hoy hubo un chico que no es muy amado que ha hecho un partidazo: Camavinga", destacó Mou tras el triunfo ante el Málaga, en la que fue la primera titularidad del 6. Desde entonces, sólo una titularidad más para él (Betis). Ante el Inter estaba sancionado y en los tres últimos encuentros, Bernardo y Tchouaméni le han ganado la partida en el once. Todo ello sin que Camavinga haya conseguido alejar los fantasmas de su bajo rendimiento en su sexta temporada como madridista. Zidane le abrió la puerta de la selección y su paso está siendo positivo. Dadas las carencias en el juego del Madrid, se esperaba un mayor protagonismo del portugués para ayudar al equipo a salir del atasco futbolístico. Por exigencia física es una posición en la sufre a nivel defensivo, pero su calidad y visión de juego podían venirle de maravilla al equipo. Con esa idea arrancó Mourinho la temporada, con Valverde y Bernardo en el doble pivote en el primer partido de Liga ante el Espanyol. Pero luego el ex del City no ha tenido ninguna continuidad en los onces iniciales. Fue titular otra vez ante el Rayo en el Bernabéu y nada más. En el derbi perdió el sitio ante Tchouaméni, que había reaparecido 12 días antes frente al Inter. Otra prueba que parece no haber convencido del todo a Mourinho. La única pieza que le queda a Mourinho por probar para ver si la cosa funciona en el centro del campo. Parecía que sin Arbeloa el canterano tenía todas las papeletas para salir. De hecho, el propio Arbeloa hizo todo lo posible por ficharlo para su proyecto en el Fulham. Pero Mou hizo especial hincapié en que se lo quería quedar y el club lo sacó del mercado. Thiago es una joya que el portugués quería seguir puliendo en Valdebebas, aunque el plan lo arruinó una lesión de rodilla que lo dejó sin pretemporada. Razón por la que el técnico dio luz verde a que durante el parón el jugador se incorporase al Castilla para disfrutar de minutos y recuperar el terreno perdido a nivel de competición. Una 'pretemporada' exprés para que se ponga al mismo nivel que el resto de los jugadores por los que compite por un puesto. A la vuelta del parón puede ser la hora de Thiago Pitarch.

articles.title: Ian Murray: Greenock Morton manager leaves Scottish Championship bottom side
articles.summary: Manager Ian Murray leaves Greenock Morton with the club bottom of the Scottish Championship.
articles.body:
Manager Ian Murray has left Greenock Morton with the club bottom of the Scottish Championship.

Coach Bill Orr has also departed Cappielow and first-team player Michael O'Halloran and assistant manager Gary Miller will take charge in the interim.

Morton have one point from their opening eight league fixtures, three points fewer than second-bottom Queen's Park. The Greenock side host Raith Rovers on Saturday.

One of Morton's sponsors has encountered difficulties, having a knock-on effect on the club's finances and recruitment this season.

Former Hibernian, Rangers and Scotland player Murray, 45, has previously managed Dumbarton, St Mirren, Airdrieonians and Raith Rovers and took over at Cappielow in January. He won four of 29 games in charge.

A club spokesperson said: "The board of Greenock Morton Football Club can confirm that Ian Murray has been relieved of his duties as first-team manager with immediate effect. First-team coach Bill Orr has also been relieved of his duties.

"We would like to place on record our sincere thanks to both Ian and Bill for their hard work, commitment and professionalism during their time at the club. Everyone at Morton wishes them both the very best for the future.

"The club recognises the disappointment felt by supporters and understands the importance of the weeks ahead."

articles.title: Olivia Holdt: Tottenham forward on second place in the WSL, tough London City, Chelsea and Arsenal tests, and life under Martin Ho
articles.summary: Watch Tottenham vs London City Lionesses in the WSL live on Sky Sports Football from 1.30pm on Sunday; kick-off 2pm; watch free in-game clips and match highlights shortly after full-time on Sky Sports' digital platforms
articles.body:
One of the players who helped do that is Olivia Holdt. When she joined the club in January 2025 under former boss Robert Vilahamn, he described her as having the 'X-factor' and the potential to be one of the best players in the league.

Big compliments, big expectations - and Holdt has certainly shown why Vilahamn described her as such, even if she is rarely in the headlines.

She has already begun this season with a hat-trick in a 7-0 thrashing of Crystal Palace - something Holdt describes as 'special' - with Spurs yet to lose in the WSL. They sit in second, three points behind Man City and a point ahead of this weekend's opponents - headline-grabbing London City.

"It's really early on, there's still a lot of games to come and it's going to be a long season, but so far, it's looking really good," Holdt exclusively said ahead of that game on Sunday, live on Sky Sports .

"There's nobody thinking it's annoying that we're second right now and we're very happy to be where we are, but it's also deserved because our performances have been really good in the first couple of games.

"I'm looking forward to Sunday. It's going to be interesting to play against London City. It hasn't gone past anyone that they've really invested coming into the season and got some really strong, good players.

"It's going to be a good game. Hopefully, we can continue our boom right now and get three points on Sunday as well."

Such a game could go some way to defining where Tottenham finish come May. So could the following two after the international break as they face Chelsea and Arsenal in successive WSL matches.

They will offer a real insight into this Spurs side. They have scored the most league goals (15) and conceded just twice, seeing the better of the possession and playing quick, attacking football. Come out of these three matches still in the top three and still leading in these metrics, Tottenham surely have to be considered as title contenders.

"It's going to be a good test for us," Holdt said. "And no disrespect to the teams that we have played, but they're maybe more of the games that we expect ourselves to get three points out of.

"So coming up against the likes of Chelsea and Arsenal, it's going to be a really good for us to see where we stand and how we can compete against them. It is a level up.

"If you look at the players, they have been at the top for many years, but whenever we play them in this season, I think we will be able to stand up for ourselves and give them a good game."

How 'mutual respect' with Ho has helped make Holdt key performer

Holdt has been one of the most consistent performers under Ho, and was Spurs' top scorer last season. She netted ten goals in all competitions, with eight in the WSL. It is clear their relationship is one that has been mutually beneficial in Spurs' success.

"He's a great coach and he's helped me a lot in getting my performances good in the league," the Denmark international said.

"I think it's his ability to give the players confidence and energy and believe in themselves. We also have a good relationship outside of the pitch as well.

"We have a mutual respect for each other. I can disagree with him and he can disagree with me. I think that's why it's worked well for us because we can be honest with each other. Martin can tell me the hard truth and I've told him not to beat around the bush.

"Sometimes it can get heated, but at the same time, we both want the best for each other and we have this mutual respect. It's good."

While Holdt has been used primarily on the right wing, she has drifted more across the middle this season compared to last, and says she is happy to play wherever Ho wants her to.

"I feel like since joining Spurs, I've played some different positions," she added. "We're trying to figure out where I can help the team most and where I can get the best out of myself.

"But at the end of the day, Martin is the one who takes the decisions, so if he wants to play me on the right wing, I'm going to do that. If he wants to play me as the 10, then I'm happily going to do that. If he wants me on the left, I can try and do my best there as well.

"I like to see myself as a versatile offensive player, so where I'm exactly positioned on the pitch doesn't really affect me that much as long as the game plan is set, and I have good players around me that can help me find my role.

"It's nice to be everywhere a bit, and maybe it makes it harder for the opposition as well. They never know where I'm going to be."

Holdt and Spurs will be hoping that is the exact case over the next few weeks as they look to maintain their disruption of the WSL order.

articles.body:
A handful of the biggest brands in college football hit the road for potentially tricky matchups in Week 5.

The Alabama Crimson Tide and Ohio State Buckeyes each have Top 20 matchups on the road within their conference against opponents with a ton to prove on the national stage.

Seven of the top 10 teams in the AP Top 25 will play on the road in Week 5.

Alabama's trip to face the Mississippi State Bulldogs is fascinating because of the quarterback battle.

Ohio State's visit to Iowa City to play the Iowa Hawkeyes kicks off a stretch of four games against ranked foes in the next five.

All of the forecasts for Week 5's college football slate can be found here on The Weather Channel.

Utah State at No. 22 Boise State (-20.5)

Schedule: 7:30 p.m. ET, CBS Sports Network

Prediction: Boise State 41, Utah State 17

You'd be hard pressed to find a better quarterback matchup than the one on display in Starkville on Saturday.

Alabama's first-year starter Keelon Russell accounted for 11 touchdowns in the first four games. The Crimson Tide eclipsed the 40-point mark in all of those contests.

Mississippi State's Kamario Taylor has taken the college football world by storm with his 14 touchdown passes and dual-threat ability.

Saturday presents Taylor and Mississippi State with a massive opportunity to announce itself as a College Football Playoff contender.

Alabama's already gone on the road and won in the SEC with Russell at the helm. The Crimson Tide used a fourth-quarter surge after a tight three quarters to beat the Kentucky Wildcats 45-17 in Week 2.

Russell likely learned a decent amount from that game about what life on the road in the SEC is like. That will be valuable to him in Starkville amid the loud clanging of the cowbells in the stands.

Alabama is the toughest defense Taylor faced in his young career. Sure, he has three wins against power-conference opponents, but none of them carried the quality of Alabama's defense.

Alabama held three of its four opponents under 20 points. Mississippi State let up 34 and 24 points in its first two SEC contests.

The quarterbacks will absolutely make some jaw-dropping plays, but the defense that gets one or two key stops will deliver the victory. Right now, the Crimson Tide have the more trustworthy unit on that side of the ball.

The Ohio State Buckeyes have one of the toughest five-week stretches in the sport upcoming.

The run that includes four Top 25 opponents begins at Kinnick Stadium against an Iowa Hawkeyes team that surged up to No. 14 following its last-second road win over the Michigan Wolverines.

Iowa is still a tier below Ohio State in the Big Ten in terms of potential playoff contenders, but its got a shot at the Buckeyes at home on Saturday.

The Hawkeyes, by the way, could be a playoff team even with a loss because they don't have any other ranked opponents on their schedule.

Iowa hasn't allowed an opponent to score over 20 points yet this season. Its defensive resolve will be tested by the Jeremiah Smith-led Buckeyes offense that scored over 40 points on three occasions.

Ohio State needs a win in Iowa City to kick off a stretch that includes trips to face the Indiana Hoosiers and USC Trojans and the Oregon Ducks at home.

The winning formula could be something as simple as overwhelming Iowa with Smith, Bo Jackson and the rest of the star power inside the Ohio State offense.

Smith put up over 150 receiving yards in three of his four games and is coming off a four-touchdown performance. He's borderline unstoppable at the moment, even for an Iowa defense that is typically sound as a unit.

Iowa might not be able to slow down Smith for four quarters, but it has the potential to contain him for stretches of the game, which is why the Hawkeyes are a fascinating underdog on the spread.

The Hawkeyes are capable of keeping the game within two scores, and as long as the spread hangs a half-point over 14, it's worth biting at Iowa to cover.

articles.title: Expert CFB Locks for Mississippi State vs. Alabama and Week 5's Biggest Games
articles.summary: After a month of football, we've learned plenty.
articles.body:
After a month of football, we've learned plenty.

The SEC is loaded, whether you want to believe it or not. Miami has reloaded, even though the schedule has been, well, underwhelming. Lincoln Riley still can't win big games, which pretty much speaks for itself.

Oh, and a bet is never truly won until the final second is off the clock.

For further proof, just look at what happened at Tennessee and Michigan a week ago. The favorites, Texas and Michigan, were cruising toward covers. Then college football things happened, as they often do.

As for our weekly picks against the spread, we're looking forward to a massive month. September had some ups, but it was also packed with bad beats. This stretch will be ripe with winners. It's a matter of time.

NFL scouts, take note. Two electric QB prospects seemingly destined for the 2028 draft will duke it out, and the winner will likely firmly entrench themselves at or near the top of the Heisman conversation.

In terms of football stories, Mississippi State has a lot working for it. QB Kamario Taylor has been sensational, accounting for 15 touchdowns in just four games. He's become a star seemingly overnight, dazzling with spectacular deep balls each and every week.

Keelon Russell has been just about as sensational, showing his arm and legs in the Crimson Tide's first four games. He struggled in the first half of Alabama's road game to Kentucky, although he eventually settled in.

That experience feels significant. Playing on the road in Starkville, with cowbells echoing throughout the stadium, presents a real challenge. At the very least, Russell has been in that kind of environment before and knows how to manage the potential jitters.

As for the rest of the team, neither defense should slow down either quarterback. It just feels like Alabama's talent across the roster, coupled with Russell's rapid development, will be the difference.

To say Shane Beamer's seat is hot would be an understatement. Presently, with the team's best defensive player suspended and South Carolina's season on the brink of collapse, it's on fire.

The Gamecocks were thoroughly beaten by Alabama, with both the offense and defense struggling. Defensive star Dylan Stewart was later suspended following an on-field incident in which he punched an opposing player's helmet. His conduct also appeared to frustrate South Carolina's coaching staff, including Beamer.

So why are we doing this? Are we running toward the fire rather than away from it?

Well, it's what we do, of course. We tend to look at things from a slightly contrarian point of view, and that's likely how the public will see it.

Kentucky is ranked, playing solid football and looking much better than we expected it to. Still, given Texas A&M's struggles, beating the Aggies on the road doesn't look quite as impressive a few weeks later.

That's not to take anything away from Will Stein; he's been as advertised and then some. But winning on the road can be challenging, and the talent South Carolina has on its roster is still robust.

This one will be ugly. You have been warned.

We were on the Cyclones last week against Utah, and it was an emotional roller coaster.

For a while it was very bad. Then, things looked very good. Then, at the very end, the implosion finally arrived.

Iowa State deserves credit for coming back after falling behind 17-0. The end result, however, was essentially the same.

West Virginia knows the feeling, only the script was flipped. After jumping out to a double-digit lead, Oklahoma State took over. Perhaps more concerning for the Mountaineers, however, is the Pokes finished with more than 600 total yards.

Presently, West Virginia has the nation's No. 84 scoring defense. And now it will play its first road game of the season, visiting an environment that remains a challenge for opponents.

QB Jaylen Raynor has to play better for Iowa State, as does the offensive line. If they can avoid turnovers, they should come away with a win.

Life in the SEC can be difficult. It just means more, after all.

While that slogan can be tiresome, it carries some truth in 2026. The conference is deep, the emotional swings are massive and things evolve.

Florida doesn't need to look far and wide to understand this. Just look at what Ole Miss had to deal with last week, one Saturday removed from taking down former head coach Lane Kiffin and LSU.

Now, Florida must hit the road with a football hangover. Granted, playing at Missouri isn't as difficult as playing in The Swamp, but it's still a fascinating test for a team still trying to figure out exactly what it is.

For Missouri, it must find a way to rebound. The Tigers came up short against Mississippi State on the road on Saturday in a close game. It's a game, quite frankly, they could have and should have won.

Either way, playing at home will do this team well. Playing on the road could challenge Florida, especially if Missouri can contain Jadan Baugh and that explosive Gators run game.

We made our thoughts of Lincoln Riley known in the introduction, and those thoughts haven't changed. His teams have struggled in big games, and that theme continued against Oregon last week.

But this game, while by no means small, should suit USC well. While the Trojans showcased some warts against Oregon last week, in particular with the Ducks' starting QB unable to play for much of the game, this team still offers plenty on the offensive side.

For Washington, this season just hasn't looked quite right. The Huskies lost outright to Minnesota, and they struggled against Washington State and Utah State earlier in the year.

It's hard to know what exactly has happened with the team's offense, although none of it feels quite right. Quarterback Demond Williams Jr. hasn't exactly dazzled, although the problems are much bigger than him.

This feels like a get-right game for the Trojans. The offense should hum, and the team should look different than the one we saw last week. After this week, well, all bets are off.

We'll cross that bridge when we get there.

While the early portion of the season can lie, Wake Forest's dramatic improvement seems very real. And although Stanford was kind to the bank account last week, this is a long road trip and a tough matchup.

Mike Norvell needs this game and then some. Perhaps that's putting it mildly. As for the teams, FSU has played tough competition; Virginia has yet to play on the road. The Seminoles pull off a mild upset.

A 4-0 team is less than a touchdown favorite against a program with one win? That would be correct. Still, Temple has played a competitive schedule and competitive games. Look out here.

Oh, this line spoke to me. TCU, which hasn't played all that well, is getting less than a touchdown against BYU. The public is likely to be all over the Cougars, which means we're going the other way.

articles.title: Ivan Toney: England forward pleads not guilty to assault charge in court following nightclub incident
articles.summary: Ivan Toney was originally charged on July 31 and is accused of attacking a man at a nightclub in central London last December; the England forward denies the charges
articles.body:
Toney stood in the dock at Westminster Magistrates' Court to confirm his name and age, and issue his not guilty plea to an incicient that happended on December 6 at a Soho club, where he is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva.

The 30-year-old, wearing a black top over a shirt and tie, was accompanied by three members of his entourage as he arrived at court shortly after 9.30am.

The criminal case came after an investigation by London's Metropolitan Police and the charge was announced in late July.

In a statement, his spokesperson said: "Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court."

He was freed on unconditional bail until a hearing in front of a judge and jury at London's Southwark Crown Court on October 29.

Toney represented England at this summer's World Cup and has 10 international appearances and one goal, but missed out on the latest squad for the country's Nations League ties.

Toney started his football career with Northampton Town and played for teams including Wigan Athletic and Peterborough United before signing for Brentford in 2020.

He scored 72 goals during four years with the Bees before making a surprise switch in 2024 to Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli.

articles.title: Arsenal: Was penalty after Leah Williamson handball the correct decision in Champions League?
articles.summary: Arsenal defender Leah Williamson was at the heart of a bizarre incident in their Women's Champions League draw with Paris FC.
articles.body:
A bizarre error from Arsenal defender Leah Williamson proved costly in their 2-2 draw with Paris FC on Wednesday in the Women's Champions League.

With the Gunners leading 2-1 late on, England captain Williamson stopped a short goal-kick with her hand - believing it had not been taken and that she was to take it - resulting in a penalty being awarded to the hosts, converted by Maeline Mendy.

The unusual incident means the Gunners are fourth in the Champions League table after their opening two games, but would have been second with a victory in the French capital.

After the ball had gone out of play for a goal-kick, Arsenal goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez played a quick, short pass to Williamson.

Williamson had her arm stretched out to stop the ball and place it so that she could take the goal-kick herself.

With the ball being still and on the field of play when Rodriguez played the ball to Williamson, that was deemed to be the goal-kick instead of Williamson's attempt.

Therefore Williamson was penalised for handball and Mendy levelled the match from the penalty spot.

While Arsenal felt aggrieved at the decision, the guidance on such incidents state that the decision to award a penalty was correct.

Guidance from Law 16 of the International Football Association Board's (Ifab) laws of the game state: "In goal-kick restarts, if the ball is stationary within the goal area and is kicked by any defending player, the goal-kick is considered to have been taken.

"If, after the ball is in play, [a player] commits a handball offence, a penalty kick is awarded if the offence occurred inside the kicker's penalty area.

Law 12 from Ifab also states: "It is an offence if a player deliberately touches the ball with their hand/arm."

In November 2024, Aston Villa defender Tyrone Mings committed an identical error in a Champions League match against Club Brugge.

Brugge won a penalty that was scored by Hans Vanaken, with the Belgian side winning the match 1-0.

"The biggest mistake I witnessed in my career," said Villa boss Unai Emery at the time.

Earlier that year, Gunners centre-back Gabriel also made the mistake in a Champions League match against Bayern Munich.

However in that instance, Arsenal were given the chance to retake the goal-kick.

"He [Gabriel] touched the ball with the hand because he thought it was not in game, but it was in game and the referee admitted it was in game and was handball," said then Bayern boss Thomas Tuchel.

The now England head coach also said that the error in not awarding Bayern a penalty was a "kid's mistake".

Arsenal's assistant coach Aaron D'Antino conducted post-match media duties and explained that, while the intention was for Williamson to take the goal-kick, they will use the incident as a learning experience.

"If we're looking at what we can control, it's just passing the ball to Leah from what I remember seeing. The ball was still rolling and she [Rodriguez] was moving it to Leah for her to take the goal-kicks as we normally do," said D'Antino.

"So maybe the learning in that is how we get the ball to Leah, so we don't put ourselves in that situation."

Former Arsenal and Scotland defender Jen Beattie felt the referee Iuliana Demetrescu got the decision wrong, despite the correct applications of the laws.

"For me, I just don't even know how that happens. Leah knows it's a goal-kick, she's catching the ball. That's shocking from the referee," Beattie told Paramount+.

"I would have been fuming and I would have been embarrassed if they gave that. This is not what they're trying to do. It's just beyond frustrating that that's how they've tied the game.

"Leah's obviously going [to do that] because she's going to take the goal-kick, not because she's worried about the press or trying to change it - or panicking in any situation. Leah Williamson doesn't panic in those moments, she knows what she's doing. The goalkeeper knows what she's doing as well.

articles.title: Hull City's Lucas Gourna-Douath crashes near training ground
articles.summary: The crash, involving Lucas Gourna-Douath, follows a similar incident involving Sorba Thomas.
articles.body:
A Premier League player has been involved in a car crash near Hull City's training ground weeks after a similar incident involving his teammate.

A black Mercedes, which the BBC understands belongs to midfielder Lucas Gourna-Douath, 24, crashed on Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham, East Yorkshire.

Pictures of the scene show the car on its side. One resident told the BBC that the vehicle had also struck and damaged her car.

Hull City said the club was "aware of images circulating on social media following a road traffic accident near the training ground and can confirm that no one was harmed in the incident".

Humberside Police said emergency services were called at 08:30 GMT.

In September, Gourna-Douath's team-mate Sorba Thomas was involved in a crash on the same road.

Paul Nickerson, who lives on the road from where the incident took place, said: "I arrived just after it turned over because I heard the noise.

"If it had happened a minute before, my wife was walking down the road with our kids taking them to school. So, it's really worrying."

Tracy Evans, who has lived on the road for 19 years, said she has been asking for the speed limit to be reduced for about 10 years.

She said: "At that time, children are coming, going to school, the parents are coming back."

She added measures needed to be put in place "to avoid something happening in the future".

articles.title: Pablo Hernández señala al entrenador que más le ha influido
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Castellón explica en La Pizarra por qué Bielsa fue el técnico que más le influyó y qué ha tomado del argentino para construir su propia idea
articles.summary: El técnico del Castellón explica en La Pizarra por qué Bielsa fue el técnico que más le influyó y qué ha tomado del argentino para construir su propia idea
articles.body: Pablo Hernández está disfrutando de sus primeros años en los banquillos. El entrenador del Castellón pasó por La Pizarra, donde conversó con Adrián Blanco, Álex de Llano y Nahuel Miranda sobre el gran inicio de su equipo, su manera de entender el fútbol y las influencias que han marcado su todavía corta trayectoria como técnico. El Castellón ha comenzado con seis victorias y un empate, un arranque que incluso ha sorprendido al propio Pablo Hernández. "Creíamos que nos iba a costar un poco más en cuestión de puntos y de sensaciones", reconoció. Más allá de la clasificación, destacó especialmente "las sensaciones que está dando el equipo" y la adaptación de los numerosos fichajes. Durante su carrera como futbolista pasó por las manos de entrenadores como Unai Emery, Michael Laudrup, Paco Jémez o Marcelo Bielsa. Si tiene que quedarse con una influencia por encima del resto, Pablo Hernández lo tiene claro. "Te diría que el que más me ha influido yo creo que ha sido Marcelo Bielsa por su manera de ver el fútbol", explicó. Su etapa con el argentino llegó, además, en sus últimos años como jugador, cuando ya observaba los entrenamientos desde una perspectiva diferente: "Ya tienes más experiencia, intentas ya ver un poco más el porqué de las cosas". Pablo, sin embargo, no ha copiado completamente la metodología de Bielsa. Sí ha incorporado un elemento fundamental: "El concepto de la intensidad en los entrenamientos es algo que sí que cogí y que intento implantar". Su fórmula busca sesiones cortas e intensas, pero con diferencias respecto a las que vivió como futbolista: "Intento que sea un poco más con balón todo, más ameno, más divertido, con más participación de los jugadores". Y explicó el motivo: "Esa metodología a lo mejor es un poco mentalmente agotadora para los jugadores. Es muy exigente, muchas veces en los entrenamientos no te divertías". Eso sí, también recordó sus resultados: "Cuando ibas el fin de semana a los partidos, veías que volabas, que jugabas bien, que eras físicamente superior a los rivales". Pablo Hernández también dejó clara la personalidad que quiere imprimir a sus equipos. Aunque reconoce que observa y aprende de otros entrenadores, no quiere renunciar a su forma de entender el juego. "Yo tengo una idea muy clara de cómo quiero que juegue mi equipo. Intento llevarlo a cabo, sea quien sea el rival", aseguró. Su intención es "ser yo, con mis ideas, como veo el fútbol" y trasladar al banquillo parte de lo que fue como futbolista. Hasta el punto de establecer una línea roja para su carrera: "Si algún día no me veo capaz de hacer jugar a mi equipo como yo quiero, creo que ese día me iré a casa a ver los partidos por la tele tranquilamente". Otro de los pilares del proyecto es la utilización de los datos para acudir al mercado. Pablo explicó que la metodología del propietario se basa en buena medida en "la búsqueda de los jugadores en el Big Data, en los datos". El objetivo es localizar futbolistas que encajen específicamente en su modelo: "Se analizan datos que nosotros creemos que son importantes para nuestra manera de jugar". Así pueden encontrar jugadores menos conocidos o que no hayan mostrado todo su potencial en otros contextos y que el Castellón considera que pueden crecer dentro de su propuesta. Pese a haber sumado 19 de los primeros 21 puntos, Pablo Hernández evita mirar más allá del siguiente encuentro. Preguntado directamente por la palabra ascenso, respondió: "La única palabra que estoy pronunciando esta semana es Ceuta, que es nuestro próximo rival". El entrenador reconoce que "es muy bonito lo que estamos viviendo aquí", pero pide mantener la prudencia: "Esto es muy largo". Su receta pasa por "ir paso a paso, seguir con nuestras ideas, seguir con nuestra mentalidad y sabiendo que eso nos acercará al objetivo". Además, Pablo Hernández mostró su desacuerdo con que Segunda División continúe durante los parones internacionales. "Creo que es algo que LaLiga debería replantearse", señaló, antes de explicar que "no es justo que haya equipos que pierdan varios jugadores y otros que no pierdan ninguno".

articles.title: Mastantuono se sincera: "Es feo quedarse fuera de la lista del Mundial"
articles.standfirst: El ahora futbolista de la Fiorentina confirma lo bien que se siente desde que llegó a Italia
articles.summary: El ahora futbolista de la Fiorentina confirma lo bien que se siente desde que llegó a Italia
articles.body: El ahora futbolista de la Fiorentina regresó con protagonismo en la goleada por 4-0 frente a Bolivia y aprovechó para abrirse sobre uno de los momentos más duros de la última temporada: quedarse fuera de la lista de Lionel Scaloni para el Mundial de 2026. Lejos de esconder su decepción, el exjugador de River admitió el dolor que sintió cuando conoció que no estaría entre los 26 elegidos para la cita mundialista. "Es feo quedar fuera de la lista del Mundial, pero he alentado siempre a mis compañeros y a Argentina para que lo hagan bien. Hicieron un Mundial increíble y nos dejaron a todos los argentinos orgullosos", reconoció el atacante. Sin embargo, el joven talento mira ahora hacia adelante. Con una nueva etapa abierta en la Albiceleste, Mastantuono considera que llega en un momento mucho más maduro y preparado para hacerse un hueco de forma estable en el equipo nacional. "Empieza un nuevo proceso, yo me siento bien y puedo tener una oportunidad, pero sobre todo quiero trabajar para la Selección", afirmó al volante, que reconoce cierta catarsis desde que llegó a la Fiore: "Me siento muy bien desde que fui a Italia y cambié un poco mi vida". Uno de los factores que más ha influido en su crecimiento reciente ha sido la confianza de Lionel Scaloni. El futbolista agradeció públicamente la libertad que le concede el seleccionador argentino sobre el terreno de juego y vinculó su buen momento al cambio de aires que supuso su llegada al fútbol italiano. "Él me da mucha libertad para jugar y se la agradezco. Me siento muy bien desde que fui a Italia y cambié un poco mi vida. Lo disfruté mucho", explicó. Precisamente Scaloni también quiso frenar la euforia alrededor de una generación que ilusiona a Argentina. El técnico incluyó a Mastantuono junto a jóvenes como Leonel Flores y Nico Paz dentro de ese grupo de talentos que deben crecer sin una presión excesiva. "Es un talento que hay que cuidarlo, como a Franco", subrayó el seleccionador, que pidió paciencia para que los jóvenes puedan desarrollar todo su potencial.

articles.title: Zaragoza y Teruel, un derbi aragonés inédito en Liga
articles.standfirst: El domingo se verán las caras por primera vez en la competición doméstica
articles.summary: El domingo se verán las caras por primera vez en la competición doméstica
articles.body: En los últimos años, el Real Zaragoza se ha acostumbrado a jugar contra el Huesca. Hasta la fecha era el único derbi aragonés para los maños. Sin embargo, este domingo se abre un nuevo capítulo con el Teruel. Será la primera vez que se enfrenten en Liga en toda su historia, algo inimaginable décadas atrás pero la deriva del club blanquillo lo ha hecho posible. Solo existe un precedente entre ambos equipos pero fue en Copa del Rey hace más de 40 años. Fue en 1985 cuando se vieron las caras en la competición del KO en segunda ronda. El Real Zaragoza goléo en ambos partidos. Venció 1-5 en la ida y 3-0 en La Romareda. Eran otros tiempos. El domingo, eso sí, llegan con dinámicas distintas. Los de Ibai Gómez encadenan cuatro triunfos consecutivos y son segundos en la clasificación. Buscarán su tercera victoria en el Ibercaja Estadio para intentar asaltar el liderato. El buen partido en Ibiza ha reforzado las sensaciones y no quieren parar. Mientras tanto, los turolenses también son segundos pero por abajo. Igualaron con polémica en el otro derbi aragonés frente al Huesca, donde anotaron su primer gol del curso. Necesitan una victoria que les haga cambiar el panorama. Ante el Real Zaragoza no lo tendrán sencillo pero seguro que dan un plus por ser la primera vez que vivirán un encuentro de estas características.

articles.title: Rival clubs want more than just relegation for Manchester City
articles.summary: Rival clubs want Manchester City’s punishment decided this season, and they feel relegation to the Championship would be insufficient, according to reports.P...
articles.body:
Rival clubs want Manchester City 's punishment decided this season, and they feel relegation to the Championship would be insufficient, according to reports.

There's been plenty of discussion around Manchester City this week, following the Premier League's announcement that an independent commission has found the club guilty of all charges relating to serious breaches of the competition's financial rules over a nine-season period.

The punishment for the guilty verdict hasn't yet been decided, and the Premier League have confirmed that sanctions will be handed down in a further hearing with the commission.

City seemingly intend to appeal, and they continue to maintain their innocence, but the players currently employed by the club are starting to fear relegation is a serious possibility.

As for what City's rivals want the punishment to be, Matt Hughes reports for The Guardian that a number of Premier League executives have told the publication that a points deduction to relegate the Manchester club to the Championship for a single season would be 'insufficient'.

There's clearly a desire for City to face longer-term consequences, as they'd presumably just bounce straight back up to the Premier League if they were only sent one step down the English football pyramid.

Meanwhile, Dan Roan reports for the BBC that senior football figures at other Premier League clubs want City's punishment handed down before the end of the season, quoting one club official as saying: "It benefits everyone for this to be resolved as quickly as possible."

The Premier League have introduced new rules this season, stating that an appeal hearing must be concluded within 12 weeks of the deadline for it to be submitted, with another 30 days for the panel to deliver its judgement – which would mean a decision by January 24th.

But it's unclear whether those timeframes would apply to this case, given the rules were only introduced recently and the case has been ongoing for years.

articles.title: Jaguars’ Davon Hamilton making case for All-Pro season
articles.summary: Hamilton’s eight run-stops rank second among defensive tackles, while his 17.0% run-stop rate ranks first.
articles.body:
It's no secret just how good the Jaguars' run-defense is. Last season the Jaguars ranked first in rushing yards allowed and the team has not allowed a 75-yard rusher since the 2024 season.

It's a big part of who the Jaguars are, their defensive identity; forcing takeaways and stout run-defense.

At the heart of it all is defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton . He may not put up the pressures and sacks that look sexy in the box score, but his impact is no less felt on the grass. He may just be the NFL's best run-stuffer.

Across the first three weeks, Hamilton's eight run-stops rank second among defensive tackles, while his 17.0% run-stop rate ranks first. He's a big reason as to why the Jags are allowing just 3.6 yards per carry.

His impact is truly felt, however, when comparing the Jaguars' success when he is on the field versus off it. In 2026, the Jaguars are allowing 2.77 YPC when Hamilton is on the field and 4.57 YPC when he is off it. That's nearly a two-yard difference in production.

His impact is even more noticeable in minimizing yards before contact, 1.64 per attempt on the field and 3.09 off the field. His ability to eat space, close lanes, and redirect running backs is an integral part of what makes the Jags' run-defense so dominant.

Dating back to Week 1 of the 2025 season, The Jaguars allow 3.09 YPC when Hamilton sees the field. Admittedly, his impact is neutralized in the passing game, but that's not Hamilton's game, nor is it the Jaguars. Run-defense is their calling.

The Jaguars have forced 37 turnovers across the last 20 games. Add in their league-best run-defense and you've got a scary defense that forces teams into playing one-dimensional football and reaps the rewards in takeaways.

articles.title: 'Is this the end?' Cristiano Ronaldo's future with Portugal unclear after veteran star leaves team
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo’s abrupt decision to leave Portugal’s training camp after an apparent rift with coach Jorge Jesus has left many wondering about his future...
articles.body:
MADRID (AP) — Cristiano Ronaldo 's abrupt decision to leave Portugal's training camp after an apparent rift with coach Jorge Jesus has left many wondering about his future in international soccer.

Is he done with Portugal ? Or will he make peace with his coach and be back for the next international break?

There were few answers on Thursday, a day after the all-time leading scorer in men's international soccer decided to walk out on Portugal's training camp in a decision announced a few hours after Jesus said the star forward would not start the game against Denmark in the Nations League.

The 41-year-old Ronaldo, who played in his sixth World Cup this year, only said that in due course he would "tell the Portuguese people the truth about the reasons" behind his departure.

The federation also gave few details, saying only that Ronaldo left the training camp and the rest of the team would remain focused on Thursday's game against Denmark.

One possible clue: There was already a new owner of Ronaldo's famous No. 7 jersey, with Rafael Leão set to wear it on Thursday.

In Portugal, the news of Ronaldo's departure fueled speculation that the country's biggest sporting star, who had already hinted that this is his last season in soccer, would not play again for the national team.

"Is this the end?" read Thursday's front-page headline of the JM newspaper based in Ronaldo's native Madeira.

"A sad farewell," the Portuguese sports paper A Bola said.

"CR7 turns his back on the national team," read the headline on the O Jogo newspaper.

Regardless of Ronaldo's and the federation's decisions going forward, the star player could possibly face a harsh punishment for leaving the training camp.

The federation's disciplinary regulations say that any player who "abandons or fails to appear" without justification at a training session, match or activity of the national teams, or any activity related to representing the federation, "shall be sanctioned with a suspension of one to six months," in addition to a fine.

It says the "absence or abandonment shall result in the player's automatic preventive suspension."

Ronaldo did tell the federation that he was leaving, but it wasn't clear whether the decision would be considered justified in accordance with the federation's regulations.

Neither the federation nor Ronaldo's representatives immediately responded to requests for comment by The Associated Press on Thursday.

Ronaldo reportedly traveled to Madrid, his home for many years while playing for Real Madrid and where he usually stays when not playing with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia .

His social media post offered few hints about what's next.

"Following the national team coach's news conference, and after a conversation with the president of the Portuguese football federation, I decided to leave the national team's training camp," Ronaldo said.

He ended his message by saying that "now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates."

Many had been expecting Ronaldo to retire from the national team after the World Cup . And while confirmed he wouldn't appear at another World Cup, he vowed to continue playing and pursuing the milestone of 1,000 career goals. He currently stands at 979, with an international men's record of 146 goals coming for Portugal.

Ronaldo recently said that this Saudi Pro League season is likely to be the last of his professional career . Al-Nassr's next match is Oct. 9.

Coach dismisses talk of a feud with Ronaldo

Jesus, who coached Ronaldo at Al-Nassr last season when they won the Saudi Arabian league title together, took over from Roberto Martínez after Portugal's round-of-16 elimination at the World Cup. He said Wednesday in the pre-game news conference that he was not planning to start Ronaldo in the Nations League match against Denmark. But he dismissed the notion there was a feud between him and Ronaldo, and said the player told him that he would accept any decision he would make.

"It seems like there was an issue between us, but there was no issue," Jesus said before Ronaldo announced his decision to leave.

Ronaldo didn't play Sunday in Portugal's 2-1 win over Norway . He hadn't trained with the rest of the group since, sparking widespread rumors about a possible spat with Jesus. The coach said Ronaldo would practice normally on Wednesday, but he ended up deciding to leave.

Jesus acknowledged that someone with the stature of Ronaldo deserved a different type of attention from coaches, but emphasized that the "rules are the same for everyone."

Jesus admitted that he told Ronaldo that he would play at least a few minutes against Norway, but changed his mind because of the game's circumstances. He said he's the one making the team choices and "no player will ever make a decision for me."

He said it was a mistake to send Ronaldo to warm up for as long as he did, and then not use him against Norway. Jesus added that "any player" would be upset about that.

Ronaldo started in Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales last Thursday but was substituted in the 67th minute. On Tuesday, he posted on Instagram a photo of him wearing the kit accompanied by the country's flag and a heart emoji.

articles.title: New 2027 NFL Draft Big Board Drops by ESPN Expert, Arch Manning, Jeremiah Smith, More Ranked
articles.summary: Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has taken a step closer to cementing himself as a top 2027 NFL draft prospect with a historic start to the college football season.
articles.body:
Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has taken a step closer to cementing himself as a top 2027 NFL draft prospect with a historic start to the college football season.

ESPN's Jordan Reid ranked Smith as the top prospect in the upcoming NFL draft in his latest 2027 draft rankings .

The rankings are based on Reid's scouting and conversations with other NFL scouts, according to Reid.

Expert CFB Locks for Week 5's Biggest Games 🔒

Here's a look at how Reid ranked some of the other top players in the projected 2027 draft class.

B/R NFL scouts similarly ranked Smith, Moore and Simmons as the draft's top three prospects, as well as Baugh as the draft's highest-ranked running back on their latest Big Board .

Reid noted each of these top prospects have aspects of their game he feels the players could improve down the stretch of the season.

Smith could make sharper changes of direction, while Moore could "improve his discipline and hand timing at the top of routes," Reid reported. He added Simmons could develop more "consistent counter moves" and Baugh could work on his pass protection.

B/R NFL scouts listed Miami quarterback Darian Mensah at No. 4 on their latest big board, while Reid had no quarterbacks listed among his top 10 prospects.

The highest-ranked quarterback on Reid's list was Oklahoma State signal caller Drew Mestemaker, who came in at No. 11. Red described Mestemaker as a "streaky passer" with "plenty of 'wow' moments."

Mestemaker was followed on Reid's list by Mensah (No. 14), Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss (No. 16), Texas' Arch Manning (No. 17) and Oregon's Dante Moore (No. 20).

Some of these signal callers will likely go higher than their prospect rankings should quarterback-needy teams end up at the top of the NFL draft.

Players will until then continue working on improving their draft stock as Week 5 of the college football season begins Thursday.
